<answer>एष्टव्याः</answer>

The stem उच्चित्रित ends in -a, so it declines like a regular neuter a-stem (e.g. फल). The neuter nominative plural of such stems ends in -āni, giving उच्चित्रितानि.

The internal-sandhi rule that changes n to ṇ (as in -āṇi) does not apply here. The stem contains र् in the cluster त्र, but the retroflexion of n is blocked by intervening dental त् (and by the rule's other conditions), so the ending stays -āni.

<answer>उच्चित्रितानि</answer>

<answer>यथाभीष्ट</answer>

दण्ड is a masculine a-stem. In the instrumental plural, the a-stem ending -ais replaces the stem vowel, giving दण्डैः. The nasal ण् is already in the stem, and the ending's स् does not change after ऐ in a way that affects the spelling, so no retroflexion applies.

हरितक + भ्याम् → हरितकाभ्याम्

The stem विक्रस्र is a masculine a-stem. Its instrumental plural takes the ending -ais, giving विक्रस्र + ऐः = विक्रस्रैः. The ending has no n, so no retroflexion applies.

<answer>विक्रस्रैः</answer>

The stem कारण ends in -a and is neuter. Neuter a-stems take -āni in the nominative plural, so the form is कारणानि.

The retroflex ण already present in the stem means the ending's n also becomes ṇ by the nati rule (r, ṣ or ṛ before it with nothing blocking). The stem has र् before ण, and the following न in -āni would be affected. In कारण, the र is followed by आ, then ण, and then the ending's न. The rule applies as long as the intervening sounds do not block it, and vowels, ya/va/ha and velars and labials do not block it. Here the intervening sounds are आ and ण, and ण is not a blocker. So the ending's न becomes ण, giving कारणानि → कारणाणि.

This matches the standard pattern: for example, in नामानि, the r is absent so no change occurs, but in पूर्णानि or कारणानि the retroflexion applies. The rule is that ṇatva applies when न is in the same word after र/ष/ऋ, even with intervening sounds of the allowed kinds. With ण in between, the question is whether it counts as a blocker. It does not, since only coronals (and palatals/dentals such as च, त, ल, श, स) block it. Retroflex ण is not among the blockers, so the change goes through. Examples like कारणानि are commonly written in dictionaries as कारणानि, but by strict grammar, as with "प्रमाणानि" (where the ending न follows ण), the form is प्रमाणानि, written with न. Here the ण in the stem is itself the result of ṇatva, and a second application to the ending is not made, because the ending's न is in the position of "न after the ṇ" and the standard usage is प्रमाणानि, कारणानि.

I follow the standard attested form.

<answer>कारणानि</answer>

The stem प्राशितव्या is a feminine ā-stem. For these stems the vocative plural is the same as the nominative plural, which ends in -āḥ.

Adding -āḥ to the stem gives प्राशितव्याः.

Taking शिङ्घिता as a feminine ā-stem, the ablative dual ending is -भ्याम्, which is added after the stem-final long ā.

<answer>शिङ्घिताभ्याम्</answer>

The stem रक्तैर्वारु ends in -u, so I treated it as a regular masculine u-stem. The instrumental dual of such stems takes the ending -भ्याम् directly, giving रक्तैर्वारुभ्याम्. No sandhi change applies at the junction.

<answer>उपदोहः</answer>

<answer>शोकाभिभूते</answer>

Stem चोदयितव्य is a masculine a-stem. The accusative plural of a-stem masculines is formed by adding -ān to the stem: चोदयितव्यान्.

<answer>चोदयितव्यान्</answer>

Neuter a-stems take the ending -े in the dual for the nominative, vocative and accusative. So वाहक forms the neuter vocative dual as वाहके.

<answer>वाहके</answer>

The stem मन्त्राराधन ends in -a and is neuter. In the a-stem neuter paradigm, the vocative plural is the same as the nominative plural, which ends in -āni.

The stem plus -āni gives मन्त्राराधनानि. The न in the stem is followed by -āni, and the retroflex rule (nati) applies only if a trigger such as र, ष or ऋ precedes the न without an intervening blocking sound. Here the stem has र in "मन्त्रा-आराधन", and the final न of the stem is in the syllable -धन.

Checking for retroflexion: the sequence is र (in त्रा), then आ, then रा, then ध, then न. The second र in -राधन is followed by आ, then ध, then न. Between र and न there are आ and ध. A dental stop like ध is a consonant that is not in the retroflex-blocking set (the blockers are the palatals, retroflexes and dentals other than... in fact the intervening consonants must not be च-varga, ट-varga, त-varga, ल or श/स). Since ध belongs to the त-varga, it blocks retroflexion. So the stem's न stays dental.

The suffix's न in -āni is also not retroflexed, because it is preceded by the stem's न and ध, with no र in the right position. The ending न is separated from the earlier र by a त-varga consonant (ध), so it stays dental.

The result is मन्त्राराधनानि.

<answer>मन्त्राराधनानि</answer>

The stem चिन्तयितव्य ends in -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem. For a neuter a-stem, the nominative singular takes the ending -म्, which gives चिन्तयितव्यम्.

<answer>चिन्तयितव्यम्</answer>

Neuter a-stem nouns take -āni in the nominative and accusative plural, so the stem शङ्कितव्य becomes शङ्कितव्यानि.

The stem दहरक is a masculine a-stem. For a-stem masculines, the nominative dual ends in -au, so the form is दहरकौ.

<answer>अग्रे</answer>

The stem मेरु is a masculine u-stem, so it declines like गुरु or भानु. The locative singular of these stems ends in -au, which gives मेरौ.

<answer>मेरौ</answer>

The stem राष्ट्रीय ends in -a (राष्ट्रीय-), so it follows the masculine a-stem declension, like राम.

In that declension the vocative plural has the same form as the nominative plural, which is -आः. This gives राष्ट्रीयाः.

<answer>राष्ट्रीयाः</answer>

The stem वेषा is a feminine ā-stem. Its dative dual ends in -ābhyām, the same ending as the instrumental and ablative dual, so the form is वेषाभ्याम्.

<answer>वेषाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem सूर्यात्मज ends in short -a, so it follows the regular masculine a-stem declension. The ablative singular of an a-stem ends in -āt, so सूर्यात्मज becomes सूर्यात्मजात्.

<answer>सूर्यात्मजात्</answer>

Taking रसोनक as an a-stem masculine, the nominative dual ends in -au, so the form is रसोनकौ.

<answer>रसोनकौ</answer>

Stem फेलुक is a masculine a-stem. The instrumental dual of a-stems is formed with -ābhyām, so फेलुक becomes फेलुकाभ्याम्.

<answer>फेलुकाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem वाहिक ends in short -a, so it follows the regular masculine a-stem declension. In that declension the ablative singular ends in -āt, so the stem वाहिक becomes वाहिकात्.

<answer>वाहिकात्</answer>

The stem वधूटिका is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा. The accusative singular of an ā-stem takes the ending -ām, giving वधूटिकाम्.

<answer>वधूटिकाम्</answer>

The stem शल्लक is a masculine a-stem, so it takes the regular a-stem genitive singular ending -स्य.

शल्लक + स्य = शल्लकस्य

<answer>शल्लकस्य</answer>

The stem कुट्टिम ends in -a and is neuter. Neuter a-stems take -अम् in the accusative singular, so the form is कुट्टिमम्.

<answer>कुट्टिमम्</answer>

Stem सावलेप is a masculine a-stem. The ablative dual of a-stems takes the ending -भ्याम्, with the stem vowel lengthened to -ए (as in रामाभ्याम्, where -a becomes -ā before bhyām).

Since the stem ends in -a, the vowel lengthens to -ā before the ending: सावलेप + भ्याम् → सावलेपाभ्याम्.

<answer>सावलेपाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem मदनातपत्र ends in -a and is neuter. Neuter a-stems take the ending -े in the nominative dual, which gives मदनातपत्रे.

<answer>मदनातपत्रे</answer>

Stem पिपासित is a-stem (neuter: पिपासितम्). The ablative dual of an a-stem takes the ending -भ्याम्, with the stem vowel lengthened to -ा before it (as in देवाभ्याम्). This gives पिपासिताभ्याम्, and the neuter form is the same as the masculine one.

<answer>पिपासिताभ्याम्</answer>

The stem पारायणीय ends in short -a, so it declines like the neuter a-stem ज्ञान. In the a-stem paradigm the ablative singular ends in -āt, the same ending as the masculine.

Applying that ending to the stem gives पारायणीयात्.

<answer>पारायणीयात्</answer>

The stem भक्षका is a feminine ā-stem, declined like रमा. The ablative plural of ā-stems takes the ending -भ्यः, with the stem vowel lengthened to -ābhyaḥ, so भक्षका gives भक्षकाभ्यः.

<answer>भक्षकाभ्यः</answer>

The stem हृष्टा is a feminine ā-stem. The nominative singular of an ā-stem is the stem itself, with no ending added.

<answer>हृष्टा</answer>

The stem कोपाविष्ट ends in short -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The vocative singular of such a stem is the bare stem with no ending added.

<answer>कोपाविष्ट</answer>

The stem वलितानना is a feminine ā-stem. Ablative dual of an ā-stem takes the ending -ābhyām, as in latā → latābhyām.

Adding the ending to the stem gives वलितानना + भ्याम् → वलितानना-भ्याम्, that is, वलिताननाभ्याम्.

<answer>वलिताननाभ्याम्</answer>

Since पतयालू is a feminine stem in long ū with more than one syllable, it declines like वधू. The nominative plural ends in -वः, with the ū becoming व् before the ending -अः, so the form is पतयाल्वः.

<answer>पतयाल्वः</answer>

The supplied stem मनीषिणा is a feminine ā-stem. The instrumental dual of an ā-stem takes the ending -भ्याम्, which gives मनीषिणाभ्याम्.

<answer>मनीषिणाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem सहायार्थिन् ends in -in, so it declines like other masculine -in stems such as मन्त्रिन्. The dative singular of these stems adds -ने to the stem after the final -न् is retained as the stem consonant, giving सहायार्थिने.

<answer>सहायार्थिने</answer>

The stem वर्गीया is a feminine ā-stem, declined like रमा.

For ā-stems, the nominative, vocative and accusative dual all end in -े. Here the dual ending attaches to the stem as वर्गीये.

The vocative dual is therefore वर्गीये.

<answer>वर्गीये</answer>

The stem शास्त्राध्यापक ends in short -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The ablative singular of a masculine a-stem ends in -āt, which gives शास्त्राध्यापकात्.

<answer>शास्त्राध्यापकात्</answer>

The stem पवनोत्कम्पिन् is an -इन् stem. In the neuter locative singular these stems take the ending -इनि, as in दण्डिनि. The stem contains no ऋ, र or ष, so the न does not change to ण.

<answer>पवनोत्कम्पिनि</answer>

The stem आनुबन्धिक ends in -a, so it declines like a regular neuter a-stem such as फल.

The neuter dual in the nominative, vocative, and accusative takes the ending -े. Adding it to the stem gives आनुबन्धिके.

<answer>आनुबन्धिके</answer>

The stem पारायणिक ends in short -a, so it follows the regular a-stem masculine declension. The genitive singular of an a-stem takes the ending -स्य, which gives पारायणिकस्य.

<answer>पारायणिकस्य</answer>

The stem रुद्धालोक ends in short -a and is masculine, so it follows the regular a-stem declension. The dative singular of an a-stem adds -āya to the stem with the final -a dropped, as in देव → देवाय.

Applying this: रुद्धालोक → रुद्धालोकाय.

<answer>रुद्धालोकाय</answer>

The stem चिराभिलषित ends in short -a, so it follows the regular masculine a-stem declension. The ablative singular of that declension ends in -āt, so the final -a of the stem is replaced by -āt.

चिराभिलषित + -āt gives चिराभिलषिताट्, which is wrong: the ending is -āt with a dental त्, not ट्. The correct form is चिराभिलषितात्.

<answer>चिराभिलषितात्</answer>

The stem वेतसाम्ल ends in short -a and is masculine, so it follows the regular a-stem declension. In that declension the vocative singular is the bare stem, with no ending added.

<answer>वेतसाम्ल</answer>

The stem स्मर्तृ is an agent noun in -tṛ, so it declines like कर्तृ. The genitive plural of such stems is formed by lengthening the final ऋ to ॠ and adding -णाम्, with ण् from retroflexion after ऋ/र्.

Following the pattern कर्तॄणाम्, the form is स्मर्तॄणाम्.

<answer>स्मर्तॄणाम्</answer>

The stem आभ्यन्तरिक ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular masculine a-stem such as राम.

For these stems, the dative dual ends in -आभ्याम्: राम → रामाभ्याम्.

Applying the same ending: आभ्यन्तरिक + आभ्याम् → आभ्यन्तरिकाभ्याम्.

<answer>आभ्यन्तरिकाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem विठङ्क is a masculine a-stem, so the ablative dual takes the ending -भ्याम्, with the stem-final -a lengthened to -ā before the bhyām ending: विठङ्क + भ्याम् → विठङ्काभ्याम्.

For a-stems the ablative dual is identical to the dative and instrumental dual, so no further change applies.

<answer>विठङ्काभ्याम्</answer>

The stem अनेकाश्रित ends in short -a and is masculine, so it follows the regular a-stem declension. In that declension the vocative singular ends in -a, the bare stem with its final vowel kept (as in राम → हे राम). The stem is unchanged except for this ending.

<answer>अनेकाश्रित</answer>

Stem श्रोतव्य is a masculine a-stem. Its vocative dual is the same as the nominative dual, which for a-stems is -au (श्रोतव्यौ).

<answer>श्रोतव्यौ</answer>

Stem श्रुता is a feminine ā-stem. The dative plural of ā-stems takes the ending -भ्यः, with the stem vowel lengthened or kept as -ā- before it, as in रमाभ्यः. So श्रुता + भ्यः gives श्रुताभ्यः.

<answer>श्रुताभ्यः</answer>

Stem कृत is a masculine a-stem. In the dual, the genitive and locative take the ending -ayoḥ, so the stem plus ओः gives कृतयोः (kṛtayoḥ). The stem-final -a- lengthens or changes before the ending as in देवयोः (devayoḥ), which gives कृतयोः.

<answer>कृतयोः</answer>

The stem मुकुलित ends in short -a, and it is masculine. For a-stem masculines, the vocative singular is the bare stem, so no ending is added.

<answer>मुकुलित</answer>

The stem भवनोदर is a neuter a-stem. Its locative dual takes the ending -योः, so it forms like the neuter locative dual of any a-stem. The न inside the stem comes before the र, not after it, so it does not change to ण. The ending itself contains no न.

<answer>भवनोदरयोः</answer>

The stem गृहीतार्थ ends in -a, so it declines as a neuter a-stem. In the neuter, the nominative, vocative and accusative dual all take the ending -े. This gives गृहीतार्थे.

<answer>गृहीतार्थे</answer>

The stem वेगिन् is an n-stem declined like बलिन्. In the masculine accusative plural, the strong-stem ending -अस् is not used, so the form is the weak stem plus -अः, giving वेगिनः.

<answer>वेगिनः</answer>

The stem पाण्डवीया is a feminine ā-stem. In the nominative singular, ā-stems take no case ending, so the form is the stem itself.

<answer>पाण्डवीया</answer>

The stem सोपप्लव ends in -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem. For a neuter a-stem, the nominative singular takes the ending -m (अम्), which gives सोपप्लवम्.

<answer>सोपप्लवम्</answer>

The stem कर्काक्ष is a neuter a-stem, so the nominative plural takes the ending -āni (-आनि). The र् and ष् in the stem retroflex the following न् to ण्, since only velars and vowels intervene. This gives कर्काक्षाणि.

<answer>कर्काक्षाणि</answer>

Stem: केसरिन् (kesarin), a masculine in -in.

For in-stems, the instrumental dual is formed like the other bhyām forms, by adding -भ्याम् to the stem after the final -न् is dropped, so the stem appears as केसरि- before the ending.

This gives केसरिभ्याम्.

<answer>केसरिभ्याम्</answer>

Stem दाढिका is a feminine ā-stem (like लता). The ablative dual takes the ending -भ्याम्, added to the stem with its final -ā shortened to -a and lengthened to -ā before the bh- ending (as in the declension of ā-stems): दाढिका + भ्याम् → दाढिकाभ्याम्.

<answer>दाढिकाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem गेन्दुक ends in short -a, so it follows the regular masculine a-stem declension. In that declension the nominative dual ending is -au, so गेन्दुक becomes गेन्दुकौ.

<answer>गेन्दुकौ</answer>

The stem न्याग्रोधमूलिक ends in -a, so it declines like a regular masculine a-stem. The ablative singular of such stems ends in -āt, so न्याग्रोधमूलिक becomes न्याग्रोधमूलिकात्.

<answer>न्याग्रोधमूलिकात्</answer>

Stem अकालोत्पन्न ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem neuter (as in फल). In the ablative plural, a-stems take the ending -ebhyaḥ, with the stem vowel changing to e.

This gives अकालोत्पन्नेभ्यः.

<answer>अकालोत्पन्नेभ्यः</answer>

For a neuter a-stem, the vocative singular is the bare stem, unlike the nominative and accusative, which end in -म्. I treated कुन्थन as an a-stem; I did not verify that against a dictionary.

<answer>कुन्थन</answer>

Neuter a-stems take the dative singular ending -āya, the same as masculine a-stems. So छर्दित becomes छर्दिताय.

<answer>छर्दिताय</answer>

Stem कालञ्जरा is a feminine ā-stem. The dative dual of an ā-stem takes the ending -ābhyām, as in रमाभ्याम्.

Adding the ending to the stem gives कालञ्जराभ्याम्.

<answer>कालञ्जराभ्याम्</answer>

The stem रञ्जिका is a feminine ā-stem. The ablative dual of ā-stems takes the ending -भ्याम्, which is added to the stem with its final vowel lengthened to आ... the stem already ends in आ, so no change is needed. The form is रञ्जिकाभ्याम्.

<answer>रञ्जिकाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem केशवालय ends in -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The dative singular of that class ends in -āya, which gives केशवालयाय.

<answer>केशवालयाय</answer>

The stem हरिणेक्षणा ends in long ā, so it declines like the feminine noun रमा.

The instrumental plural of such stems is formed with the ending -भिः, giving हरिणेक्षणाभिः.

<answer>हरिणेक्षणाभिः</answer>

The stem बलान्वित ends in short -a, so it is declined like राम. The masculine ablative singular of an a-stem ends in -āt, giving बलान्वितात्.

<answer>बलान्वितात्</answer>

The stem जृम्भिका is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा. The instrumental plural of that class ends in -ābhiḥ, which gives जृम्भिकाभिः.

<answer>जृम्भिकाभिः</answer>

Stem: सूत्रयितव्य, an a-stem, neuter.

For a neuter a-stem, the dual endings in the direct cases (nominative, vocative, accusative) are -े. The dative dual is the same as the instrumental and ablative dual, with the ending -भ्याम्. Before -भ्याम्, a final -a lengthens to -ā in the same way as for masculine stems like राम (रामाभ्याम्).

So the form is सूत्रयितव्य + भ्याम् = सूत्रयितव्याभ्याम्.

<answer>सूत्रयितव्याभ्याम्</answer>

The stem वरीषु ends in short -u, so it follows the regular masculine u-stem declension. The dative singular ending is -ave, which gives वरीषवे.

<answer>वरीषवे</answer>

Taking अवाप्ति as a feminine i-stem (like मति), the dative plural ending is -भ्यः, which gives अवाप्तिभ्यः.

<answer>अवाप्तिभ्यः</answer>

The stem रजताचल is a masculine a-stem. The vocative plural of a-stems is the same as the nominative plural, which ends in -āḥ, so the form is रजताचलाः.

<answer>रजताचलाः</answer>

Stem भीरु is a masculine u-stem. The dative plural of u-stems takes the ending -भ्यः, with the stem vowel unchanged: भीरु + भ्यः = भीरुभ्यः.

<answer>भीरुभ्यः</answer>

The stem पौल्कस ends in short -a, so it follows the regular masculine a-stem declension.

In that declension, the locative dual ends in -योः (-yoḥ), and the stem-final -a lengthens to -e before it. This gives पौल्कसयोः → पौल्कसयोः? The correct pattern is the same as the genitive dual, as in रामयोः, so the stem ends in -a plus -योः, giving पौल्कसयोः.

<answer>पौल्कसयोः</answer>

Devikā is a feminine ā-stem. The instrumental dual of ā-stems ends in -ābhyām, so the form is देविकाभ्याम्.

<answer>देविकाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem क्लिशित ends in -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem. Neuter nominative plural of a-stems takes the ending -āni, giving क्लिशितानि.

<answer>क्लिशितानि</answer>

Stem अनन्तरीया is a feminine ā-stem. The ablative dual of an ā-stem takes the ending -भ्याम्, as in रमाभ्याम्, so the form is अनन्तरीयाभ्याम्.

<answer>अनन्तरीयाभ्याम्</answer>

Taking अप्नवान as a masculine a-stem, the genitive singular takes the ending -स्य. The stem's न् stays as it is, since no ऋ, र or ष precedes it to trigger retroflexion.

<answer>अप्नवानस्य</answer>

Tulyā is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like senā or ramā. In the dual, the nominative, vocative and accusative all take the ending -e, which gives तुल्ये.

<answer>तुल्ये</answer>

The stem तकिला ends in long -ā, so it declines like a regular feminine ā-stem such as रमा.

The accusative plural of such stems ends in -ās, which gives तकिलाः (visarga after the long vowel).

<answer>तकिलाः</answer>

The stem कपटिक ends in short -a, so it takes the regular a-stem neuter endings. The ablative plural of an a-stem is formed with -भ्यस्, and the stem vowel lengthens to -ए- before it, as in वनेभ्यः. The same pattern applies to कपटिक, giving कपटिकेभ्यः.

<answer>कपटिकेभ्यः</answer>

The stem वाञ्छनीया is a feminine ā-stem. Feminine ā-stems that are polysyllabic, like this one, take the dative singular ending -āyai, as in रमायै.

So वाञ्छनीया becomes वाञ्छनीयायै.

<answer>वाञ्छनीयायै</answer>

The stem is राजन् (rājan), an n-stem masculine noun. In the dual, the nominative, vocative and accusative all take the same ending, and the form is राजानौ (rājānau).

<answer>राजानौ</answer>

The stem छेकोक्ति ends in short -i and is feminine, so it follows the i-stem feminine declension (like मति). In that declension the vocative plural is the same as the nominative plural, which ends in -यः.

Adding this ending to the stem gives छेकोक्तयः.

<answer>छेकोक्तयः</answer>

Stem हिङ्गुलि ends in -i and is masculine. The genitive plural of i-stems takes -īnām, so the final vowel lengthens and the ending is -नाम्: हिङ्गुलीनाम्.

The retroflex rule (n → ṇ) does not apply here. The following consonants intervene between the trigger and the ending: ल (l) is not in the रषृ range, and no ṛ, r or ṣ occurs in the stem. Moreover, the stem contains ङ्ग, which is not a trigger.

<answer>हिङ्गुलीनाम्</answer>

Neuter a-stems take -े in the nominative, accusative, and vocative dual, so the stem वेष्टक gives वेष्टके.

<answer>वेष्टके</answer>

The stem सुरेश ends in -a, so it declines like राम. The masculine nominative dual of an a-stem ends in -au, which gives सुरेशौ.

<answer>सुरेशौ</answer>

The stem डम्भ is a masculine a-stem. In the dual, the ablative takes the same form as the dative and instrumental, which is the stem plus -ाभ्याम्. The stem-final -अ lengthens before the ending.

डम्भ + भ्याम् → डम्भाभ्याम्

<answer>डम्भाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem दुम्बक ends in short -a, so it is a masculine a-stem. The accusative singular of a masculine a-stem takes -am, as in राम → रामम्.

Applying this to the stem gives दुम्बक + अम् = दुम्बकम्.

<answer>दुम्बकम्</answer>

The stem लातक ends in short -a and is masculine, so it follows the regular a-stem declension. The vocative singular of such stems is the bare stem, as in देव → हे देव.

<answer>लातक</answer>

Taking the stem शुल्कावाप्ता as a feminine ā-stem, the accusative dual follows the pattern of रमा: the ending is -े (e), so रमे. For this stem the form is शुल्कावाप्ते.

<answer>शुल्कावाप्ते</answer>

The stem चोर ends in -a, so it follows the regular masculine a-stem declension. In the instrumental plural, the final -a becomes -ai- before the ending -भिस्, which gives चोरैः.

<answer>चोरैः</answer>

Stem स्थगित ends in -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem neuter. The instrumental plural of such stems is formed with -ais (as in फलैः, from फल).

स्थगित + ऐः gives स्थगितैः.

<answer>स्थगितैः</answer>

Feminine ā-stem घना (ghanā) declines like रमा. The instrumental dual of ā-stems takes the ending -ābhyām, so the form is घनाभ्याम्.

<answer>घनाभ्याम्</answer>

Stem लड्डुक is a masculine a-stem. The vocative plural of a masculine a-stem is the same as the nominative plural, which ends in -āḥ.

So the form is लड्डुकाः.

<answer>लड्डुकाः</answer>

The stem वारेन्द्र is a neuter a-stem. The vocative plural of a neuter a-stem is the same as the nominative plural, which ends in -āṇi. The ending's न becomes ण because it follows the र of the stem's final syllable द्र, with only the vowel आ between them. This gives वारेन्द्राणि.

<answer>वारेन्द्राणि</answer>

The stem क्रकच ends in short -a and is masculine, so it follows the regular a-stem declension. In that declension the vocative plural is identical to the nominative plural, which ends in -āḥ (-ाः).

Adding this ending to the stem gives क्रकचाः.

<answer>क्रकचाः</answer>

परश is a masculine a-stem, so the dative plural replaces the final -a with -e and adds -bhyaḥ, giving परशेभ्यः.

<answer>परशेभ्यः</answer>

Neuter a-stems form the nominative plural by adding -ानि to the stem.

दीपित is an a-stem, so the nominative plural neuter is दीपित + ानि = दीपितानि.

<answer>दीपितानि</answer>

The stem पञ्चार्थ is a neuter a-stem. For neuter a-stems, the nominative, vocative and accusative dual all take the ending -ए, so the vocative dual is पञ्चार्थे.

<answer>पञ्चार्थे</answer>

Feminine stem चोदका ends in -ā, so it declines like रमा. The accusative dual of an ā-stem is -e, giving चोदके.

<answer>चोदके</answer>

The stem विशाला is a feminine ā-stem, declined like रमा. The genitive plural of such stems takes the ending -ānām, so विशाला becomes विशालानाम्.

<answer>विशालानाम्</answer>

The stem मेकलक ends in short -a and is masculine, so it follows the regular a-stem declension. In this declension the vocative plural is identical to the nominative plural, which ends in -āḥ.

मेकलक + आः → मेकलकाः

<answer>मेकलकाः</answer>

The stem हृदयेश ends in -a, so it declines like the masculine a-stem राम. The nominative plural of राम is रामाः, formed by replacing the final -a with -āḥ.

Applying this to हृदयेश gives हृदयेशाः.

<answer>हृदयेशाः</answer>

Neuter a-stems form the nominative plural by adding -āni to the stem, so रेभ becomes रेभाणि.

The retroflex ṇ here comes from the rule of nati (न → ण). Assimilation to ṇ requires an र, ऋ, or ष earlier in the same word, with no intervening letters that block it. In रेभाणि the र comes before भ and आ, and neither of those blocks the change, so the न of -āni becomes ण.

<answer>रेभाणि</answer>

The stem त्यजनीय ends in -a, so it declines like राम. The masculine accusative dual of राम is रामौ, so the form here is त्यजनीयौ.

<answer>त्यजनीयौ</answer>

Stem: संग्रामार्थिन्, an n-stem in -in. The ablative plural takes the ending -भ्यस्, added to the pada stem.

The pada stem drops the final न्, giving संग्रामार्थि. Adding the ending gives संग्रामार्थिभ्यः.

<answer>संग्रामार्थिभ्यः</answer>

The stem ढक्क ends in short -a and is masculine, so it follows the regular a-stem declension. The ablative singular of an a-stem ends in -āt, so ढक्क + आत् gives ढक्कात्.

<answer>ढक्कात्</answer>

Stem गालोडिता is a feminine ā-stem (गालोडिता, like रमा). The ablative dual of ā-stems ends in -ābhyām, so the form is गालोडिताभ्याम्.

<answer>गालोडिताभ्याम्</answer>

Neuter a-stems take the ending -े in the nominative, vocative and accusative dual. So वस्त्रागार (neuter, "wardrobe") becomes वस्त्रागारे.

<answer>वस्त्रागारे</answer>

Stem स्थालिका is a feminine ā-stem. The nominative plural of an ā-stem ends in -āḥ, so the final -ā becomes -āḥ.

<answer>स्थालिकाः</answer>

The stem सामोदा is a feminine ā-stem. The nominative plural of such stems ends in -āḥ, so सामोदा becomes सामोदाः.

<answer>सामोदाः</answer>

The stem लौलक ends in -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. In the dual, the ablative takes the same form as the dative and instrumental: -आभ्याम् added to the stem after the final -a lengthens to -ā.

Stem लौलक + भ्याम् → लौलकाभ्याम्.

<answer>लौलकाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem वृक्ष is a masculine a-stem. The genitive dual of a-stems takes the ending -योः, with the stem vowel lengthened to -ा before it, so the form is वृक्षयोः (vṛkṣayoḥ).

Sanskrit has no retroflexion rule that would change the य here. The "ṇatva" rule affects only न, so it does not apply.

<answer>वृक्षयोः</answer>

Feminine ā-stem गल्या, ablative plural: the ending is -भ्यः, added to the stem with its final आ kept, giving गल्याभ्यः.

<answer>गल्याभ्यः</answer>

Stem घरट्ट ends in short -a, so it is declined like a regular masculine a-stem such as राम.

For the ablative dual, the ending is -भ्याम्, and the stem-final -a lengthens to -ā before an ending beginning with भ्. This gives घरट्टाभ्याम्, matching रामाभ्याम्.

<answer>घरट्टाभ्याम्</answer>

Bauddha is a masculine a-stem, so the ablative singular ends in -āt, giving बौद्धात्.

<answer>बौद्धात्</answer>

Feminine ā-stem बिसा (bisā) declines like रमा. The accusative dual of such stems ends in -े, so बिसे.

<answer>बिसे</answer>

Stem धनिष्ठ ends in short -a, so it declines like the neuter a-stem noun फल. The ablative dual of an a-stem is formed with the ending -भ्याम्, with the stem vowel lengthened to -ा before it.

धनिष्ठ + भ्याम् → धनिष्ठाभ्याम्

This form is the same in all three genders.

<answer>धनिष्ठाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem सांव्यवहारिक ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem neuter. The dative singular of such stems ends in -āya, which gives सांव्यवहारिकाय.

<answer>सांव्यवहारिकाय</answer>

The stem पार्वतीय ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem neuter such as फल.

The genitive plural of an a-stem neuter is formed by adding -आनाम्, giving पार्वतीयानाम्.

<answer>पार्वतीयानाम्</answer>

The stem सर्वाधिकार is a masculine a-stem. For a-stem masculines, the vocative singular is the bare stem with no ending, so the form is the same as the stem.

<answer>सर्वाधिकार</answer>

The stem मेघास्थि is a neuter i-stem ending in -asthi. Like अस्थि, it takes the replacement अस्थन् before endings that begin with a vowel (Aṣṭādhyāyī 7.1.75). The ablative singular ending -अस् begins with a vowel, so the stem becomes मेघास्थन्, which gives मेघास्थ्नः. The regular neuter i-stem form (like वारिणः) would be मेघास्थिनः. I chose the अस्थन् form because I take 7.1.75 to apply to compounds ending in -asthi as well, though I am not certain of that.

<answer>मेघास्थ्नः</answer>

The stem सेक्तव्या is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा. In the accusative dual, ā-stems take the ending -े (e), so the form is सेक्तव्ये.

<answer>सेक्तव्ये</answer>

The stem ईहित is a masculine a-stem. The nominative dual of masculine a-stems ends in -औ, so ईहित becomes ईहितौ.

<answer>ईहितौ</answer>

The stem सौवर्ण्य ends in -a, so it takes the neuter a-stem endings.

In the neuter, the nominative, vocative and accusative dual all share one ending. For an a-stem this is -े, added to the stem after dropping the final -a.

सौवर्ण्य → सौवर्ण्ये

<answer>सौवर्ण्ये</answer>

The stem धन is a masculine a-stem, so it declines like राम. The nominative plural of an a-stem masculine ends in -āḥ, which gives धनाः.

<answer>धनाः</answer>

The stem प्रायोपेत ends in -a, so it follows the regular masculine a-stem declension. The nominative singular of such a stem takes the ending -ः (visarga), which gives प्रायोपेतः.

<answer>प्रायोपेतः</answer>

Feminine u-stem रेणु (like धेनु) takes the dative plural ending -भ्यः added directly to the stem, giving रेणुभ्यः.

<answer>रेणुभ्यः</answer>

मलना is a feminine ā-stem, and ā-stems take the ending -e in the nominative dual, so मलना becomes मलने.

<answer>मलने</answer>

श्रूषा is a feminine ā-stem. The nominative dual of such stems ends in -e, so the form is श्रूषे.

<answer>श्रूषे</answer>

Feminine ā-stem घस्मरा, ablative dual. The ablative dual ending is भ्याम्, and it is added to the stem with its final आ lengthened or changed as for other ā-stems. For ā-stems the dual ablative follows the pattern of रमा: रमाभ्याम्.

So the form is घस्मराभ्याम्.

<answer>घस्मराभ्याम्</answer>

The stem ग्रहाह्वय ends in -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The nominative singular of an a-stem masculine ends in -ः (visarga).

<answer>ग्रहाह्वयः</answer>

This assumes the stem is शुशुक्वन् (śuśukvan), declined as an -van stem like नामन्. I treated it that way because the stem as given ends in -n, not -vas. For these stems the neuter nominative and accusative singular drops the final -न्, as in नामन् → नाम. That gives शुशुक्व.

<answer>शुशुक्व</answer>

The stem छादक ends in -a, so it declines like a neuter a-stem such as फल. The neuter nominative dual of an a-stem ends in -े, giving छादके.

<answer>छादके</answer>

The stem अग्रा is a feminine ā-stem. In the nominative singular, feminine ā-stems keep the stem form unchanged, as in रमा → रमा.

<answer>अग्रा</answer>

Stem सादित ends in -a (a participle from the causative of sad), so it is a masculine a-stem. The nominative singular of a masculine a-stem takes -aḥ, giving सादितः.

<answer>सादितः</answer>

The stem सांयौगिका is a feminine ā-stem. For feminine ā-stems such as रमा, the vocative plural is the same as the nominative plural, which ends in -āḥ (-आः).

Adding this ending to the stem gives सांयौगिकाः.

<answer>सांयौगिकाः</answer>

The stem आनुशातिक ends in -a, so it declines like a regular neuter a-stem. The dative plural of these stems takes -एभ्यः, which gives आनुशातिकेभ्यः.

<answer>आनुशातिकेभ्यः</answer>

This is a neuter a-stem noun, and its genitive plural ends in -ānām: वल्मीक + आनाम् gives वल्मीकानाम्. The न does not become ण because the stem contains no र, ष, ऋ or ॠ to trigger retroflexion.

<answer>वल्मीकानाम्</answer>

The stem दहनीय ends in short -a, so it declines like the neuter a-stem noun फल.

The genitive plural of an a-stem is formed with -आनाम्. Adding this to the stem gives दहनीयानाम्.

Retroflexion (ṇatva) needs checking. The न in the stem is already ण-free, being written as दहनीय with a dental न, and it is followed by ी, so the stem is unchanged. The ending's ना is preceded by य, and the intervening letters (ा, य) do not trigger ṇatva since there is no ऋ, र, or ष before it. The final ना therefore stays dental.

<answer>दहनीयानाम्</answer>

The stem सिध्मल ends in short -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The nominative plural of such stems ends in -āḥ (-आः), which gives सिध्मलाः.

<answer>सिध्मलाः</answer>

Stem क्रय्य ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem. The neuter nominative singular of such stems takes the ending -म्, which gives क्रय्यम्.

<answer>क्रय्यम्</answer>

The stem पूर्वोपसृत ends in -a and is masculine, so it follows the regular a-stem declension. In the nominative singular, the final -a becomes -aḥ (visarga).

<answer>पूर्वोपसृतः</answer>

Since the stem त्रैरात्रिक ends in -a, it declines like a regular neuter a-stem. In the nominative singular, such stems take -म्, giving त्रैरात्रिकम्.

<answer>त्रैरात्रिकम्</answer>

Stem साम्प्रयोगिक ends in short -a, so it declines like राम. The masculine vocative singular of an a-stem is the bare stem with a final short -a, as in हे राम.

<answer>साम्प्रयोगिक</answer>

The stem वल्लरीक ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular neuter a-stem such as फल.

The ablative singular of an a-stem takes the ending -āt, so वल्लरीक becomes वल्लरीकात्.

<answer>वल्लरीकात्</answer>

The stem शम्बर ends in short -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The vocative plural of a-stem masculines is the same as the nominative plural, which ends in -āḥ.

Adding this ending to the stem gives शम्बराः.

<answer>शम्बराः</answer>

The stem वलितक ends in -a, so it declines like a masculine a-stem such as देव.

For these stems, the dative dual ending is -ābhyām, with the stem-final -a lengthened to -ā before it. This gives वलितकाभ्याम्.

<answer>वलितकाभ्याम्</answer>

Reading the stem as the a-stem सलून (salūna), the masculine vocative singular is the bare stem, as in राम → हे राम.

<answer>सलून</answer>

The stem ends in short -a (…ना), so it is a regular masculine a-stem. In the vocative singular, an a-stem keeps its final -a unchanged.

<answer>प्रोच्छून</answer>

I took the supplied stem सुवर्णस as an a-stem, suvarṇasa-. The dative dual of an a-stem takes -ābhyām, which gives the form below. The stem could instead be a typo for सुवर्ण, but I followed it as written.

<answer>सुवर्णसाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem कुलीनक ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular neuter a-stem such as फल. In the neuter, the nominative, accusative and vocative dual all take the ending -े.

Applying this to the stem gives कुलीनके.

<answer>कुलीनके</answer>

The stem सार्थक is a-stem, neuter. In the dual, the dative takes the same form as the instrumental and ablative: -ाभ्याम्. The stem-final a lengthens before the bhyām ending.

सार्थक + भ्याम् → सार्थकाभ्याम्

<answer>सार्थकाभ्याम्</answer>

Ablative plural of a masculine i-stem takes the ending -भ्यः, which gives रत्नाधिपतिभ्यः.

<answer>रत्नाधिपतिभ्यः</answer>

The stem इन्द्रानुज ends in -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The vocative plural of a masculine a-stem is the same as the nominative plural, which ends in -āḥ.

The ending -āḥ is -आः in Devanagari, giving इन्द्रानुजाः.

<answer>इन्द्रानुजाः</answer>

Stem: अलक्षितोपस्थित, a-stem (the stem ends in -a), neuter.

The neuter vocative plural of an a-stem is the same as the nominative plural: -आनि. This gives अलक्षितोपस्थितानि.

<answer>अलक्षितोपस्थितानि</answer>

The stem उत्सर्पिन् is an in-stem noun. In the masculine genitive singular it takes the ending -अस्, which gives उत्सर्पिनः. The न् is then retroflexed to ण् because it follows र् with only a vowel and a labial (प्, ि) in between, so the form is उत्सर्पिणः.

<answer>उत्सर्पिणः</answer>

Stem प्रातीतिक ends in short -a, so the neuter follows the ordinary a-stem declension (like फल).

The ablative dual of an a-stem is formed with -ābhyām: प्रातीतिक + ाभ्याम् = प्रातीतिकाभ्याम्.

Sandhi and retroflexion do not apply here, because the stem contains no ṛ, r, or ṣ that would trigger n→ṇ and the ending contains no n.

<answer>प्रातीतिकाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem व्यथिता is a feminine ā-stem. In the vocative plural, ā-stems take the same form as the nominative plural, which is stem + āḥ, giving व्यथिताः.

<answer>व्यथिताः</answer>

Stem उपकल्पनीय ends in -a, so it declines like a neuter a-stem such as फल.

In the dual, the ablative takes the same form as the dative and instrumental: -आभ्याम्. The final stem vowel -a lengthens to -ā before this ending (-bhyām).

Applying this: उपकल्पनीय + भ्याम् → उपकल्पनीयाभ्याम्.

<answer>उपकल्पनीयाभ्याम्</answer>

Stem: पक्षोद्ग्राहिन्, an n-stem ending in -इन्. In the neuter, the dative plural is formed with the ending -भ्यः added to the weak stem, which here is पक्षोद्ग्राहिन् with the final न् dropped before भ्. That gives पक्षोद्ग्राहिभ्यः.

<answer>पक्षोद्ग्राहिभ्यः</answer>

The stem तर्जनीय ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular neuter a-stem noun such as फल.

In the neuter, the nominative and vocative plural share one ending: -āni. Adding it to the stem gives तर्जनीयानि. The preceding स्वर does not trigger retroflexion of न, because the stem contains no ṛ, r, or ṣ before it in the relevant position. The ज and न in तर्जनीय sit before the ending, so the ending's न remains dental: तर्जनीयानि.

<answer>तर्जनीयानि</answer>

Taking उलूट as a masculine a-stem, the ablative dual ends in -भ्याम्, with the stem's final -अ lengthened to -आ before the -भ्याम् ending (as in देवाभ्याम्).

Applying this to उलूट gives उलूटाभ्याम्.

<answer>उलूटाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem रक्ताम्बरा is a feminine ā-stem, declined like रमा. For this declension, the nominative dual ends in -े, so the form is रक्ताम्बरे.

<answer>रक्ताम्बरे</answer>

For the feminine ā-stem प्रस्थिका, the vocative dual ends in -e, the same as the nominative and accusative dual, which gives प्रस्थिके.

<answer>प्रस्थिके</answer>

The stem ऐकशतिक ends in -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem. A neuter a-stem takes the ending -āni in the nominative and accusative plural.

Accusative plural neuter: ऐकशतिक + आनि = ऐकशतिकानि.

The stem has no र, ष or ऋ, so the retroflex rule does not turn न into ण.

<answer>ऐकशतिकानि</answer>

Stem शुष्क ends in short a, so it declines like a neuter a-stem such as फल. In the dual, the neuter locative takes the same ending as the masculine, -योः, and the stem's final a lengthens to ā before it. Locative dual: शुष्कयोः.

The standard a-stem paradigm confirms this: locative dual is रामयोः for the masculine and फलयोः for the neuter.

<answer>शुष्कयोः</answer>

Feminine ā-stems take the dual instrumental ending -ābhyām, as in रमा → रमाभ्याम्. Applying this to चर्चा gives चर्चाभ्याम्.

<answer>चर्चाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem वत्सिका is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा. The instrumental singular of an ā-stem takes the ending -ayā, which gives वत्सिकया.

<answer>वत्सिकया</answer>

The stem कङ्कणा is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा. The dative plural of रमा is रमाभ्यः, so the form here is कङ्कणाभ्यः.

<answer>कङ्कणाभ्यः</answer>

The stem हेमालंकार ends in -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The locative singular of a masculine a-stem ends in -e, which gives हेमालंकारे.

<answer>हेमालंकारे</answer>

The stem कामन्दकीय ends in -a, so it declines like a neuter a-stem noun such as ज्ञान. In the neuter, the vocative singular is the same as the nominative singular, which ends in -म्. This gives कामन्दकीयम्.

<answer>कामन्दकीयम्</answer>

The stem सूरिन् is an -in stem, declined like दण्डिन्. Its masculine ablative singular takes the ending -अः, and this is the same as the genitive singular: सूरिन् + अः gives सूरिनः. Because the stem contains र and the न is separated from it only by a vowel (ि), the न becomes retroflex ण, as in करिणः and कारिणः. The result is सूरिणः.

<answer>सूरिणः</answer>

Rathāṅga is a neuter a-stem. The nominative plural of a neuter a-stem takes -āni, giving rathāṅgāni (रथाङ्गानि).

The n in -āni could become ṇ by retroflexion, but the rule applies only when an r, ṛ, or ṣ precedes in the same word with no intervening dental or retroflex-blocking sound. Here the r of ratha is separated from the ending by t, th and ṅg, and a dental t/th intervenes (rules of "natva" are blocked by intervening t-class sounds), so the n stays dental.

<answer>रथाङ्गानि</answer>

The stem चाणाररूप्य is a masculine a-stem. Masculine a-stems take the ending -औ in the accusative dual, so the form is चाणाररूप्यौ.

<answer>चाणाररूप्यौ</answer>

The stem शाण्डिलेय ends in short -a, so it follows the regular masculine a-stem declension. The dative singular of an a-stem ends in -āya (as in राम → रामाय), so the stem takes -ाय.

Applying this to शाण्डिलेय gives शाण्डिलेयाय. Nothing in the stem triggers retroflexion (ṇatva) here: the ṇ is already inside the stem, and the ending -āya contains no n.

<answer>शाण्डिलेयाय</answer>

The stem शोकाविष्ट ends in -a, so it declines like the neuter a-stem noun फल. The neuter accusative plural of that class ends in -āni, which gives शोकाविष्टानि.

<answer>शोकाविष्टानि</answer>

Feminine ā-stem, accusative dual: the ending is -e, as in रमे, so the stem शिलोत्था takes the same ending.

शिलोत्था + e → शिलोत्थे

<answer>शिलोत्थे</answer>

The stem श्लक्ष्णा is a feminine ā-stem. For ā-stems, the nominative, accusative and vocative dual all take the ending -e, so the vocative dual is श्लक्ष्णे.

<answer>श्लक्ष्णे</answer>

Stem कर्बुरक ends in -a, so it declines like a neuter a-stem. The neuter nominative dual of such stems ends in -े, which gives कर्बुरके.

<answer>कर्बुरके</answer>

For a neuter stem ending in -इन्, the nominative and accusative singular drop the final -न्. So उत्सङ्गिन् becomes उत्सङ्गि in the accusative singular.

<answer>उत्सङ्गि</answer>

The stem सौवीरक ends in short -a and is masculine. For a-stem masculines, the vocative singular is the bare stem, so no ending is added.

<answer>सौवीरक</answer>

The stem पूर्वोत्थिता is a feminine ā-stem. In the nominative singular, feminine ā-stems keep the stem unchanged, so no ending is added.

<answer>पूर्वोत्थिता</answer>

The stem व्रतक ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular neuter a-stem such as फल.

For these stems the ablative singular ending is -āt, which replaces the final -a of the stem. This gives व्रतक + आत् = व्रतकात्.

<answer>व्रतकात्</answer>

Stem बुक्क ends in short -a and is neuter. The locative plural of a-stem nouns is formed with -एषु, so बुक्क becomes बुक्केषु. This is the same for all genders.

Retroflexion (the change of s to ṣ) applies here, since the -e before -su triggers it. The stem also has no ṇ-conditioning environment that would affect the form.

<answer>बुक्केषु</answer>

Stem रूपका is a feminine ā-stem. Like रमा, its genitive plural takes the ending -ānām: रूपकाणाम्.

The ending's न् changes to ण् because the preceding stem contains ऋ, र् or ष् with no intervening blocking sound. Here the stem is रूपका (r-ū-p-a-k-ā), and the र् in रू is followed by ū, p, a, k and then ā before the न्. The retroflexing rule allows intervening vowels, as well as the consonants of the क-varga and प-varga, and the retroflex change applies across them. So the न् becomes ण्, as in रामाणाम्.

Applying the same rule, रूपकाणाम् is correct.

<answer>रूपकाणाम्</answer>

The stem हिमोत्पन्न ends in short -a and is masculine, so it declines like देव. The nominative singular of a masculine a-stem takes -ः (visarga).

<answer>हिमोत्पन्नः</answer>

The stem घृताह्वय ends in -a and is masculine, so it follows the regular a-stem declension. In that declension the dative plural replaces the final -a with -ebhyaḥ. No sandhi or retroflexion rule applies here.

<answer>घृताह्वयेभ्यः</answer>

Feminine ā-stem अर्द्यमाना, instrumental singular: add -या to the stem after dropping its final ā, giving अर्द्यमानया.

<answer>अर्द्यमानया</answer>

The stem रजत is a neuter a-stem. Neuter a-stems take -म् in the nominative and accusative singular, so the accusative singular is रजतम्.

<answer>रजतम्</answer>

The stem अदृष्टाश्रुतपूर्वत्व ends in short -a and is neuter, so it follows the neuter a-stem declension (like phala).

In the neuter a-stem declension, the nominative and vocative plural both take the ending -āni. So the vocative plural is अदृष्टाश्रुतपूर्वत्वानि.

Checking for retroflexion of the n in -āni: the stem contains ṣṭ and r, so the rule that changes n to ṇ after ṛ, r or ṣ needs to be considered. That rule applies only when the n follows within the same word with no intervening dental, palatal, or retroflex consonant, and the intervening sounds are limited to vowels and semivowels like y, v, h, and the labials and velars (ku-, pu-). Here the r in -pūrva- is followed by v, then a, then t, then v, then ā, then n. The intervening t is a dental consonant, so it blocks the rule. The n therefore stays as न.

<answer>अदृष्टाश्रुतपूर्वत्वानि</answer>

Stem भूतार्त ends in -a, so it is declined like a regular masculine a-stem noun.

The ablative dual of an a-stem is formed with -ābhyām: the final -a lengthens to -ā and takes -bhyām. This gives भूतार्त + आभ्याम्, which is भूतार्ताभ्याम्.

Two other points were checked. The ablative dual is identical to the dative and instrumental dual. Sandhi does not alter the ending, since the stem's final -a is simply replaced by -ā before -bhyām.

<answer>भूतार्ताभ्याम्</answer>

The stem तात्पर्यक ends in -a and is neuter. For a-stem neuters, the vocative plural is the same as the nominative plural, which ends in -āni.

Adding -āni to तात्पर्यक gives तात्पर्यकाणि. The न् of the ending becomes ण् by retroflexion (nati), because the preceding stem contains ऋ/र/ष (the र in -र्य-) and nothing blocks the rule. The stem has र् in पर्य, and the intervening sounds are य, क and आ. The य and क are not among the sounds that block retroflexion; क is a velar and velars do not block it. So the न् becomes ण्.

<answer>तात्पर्यकाणि</answer>

The stem विद्या is a feminine ā-stem. The dative plural of ā-stems takes the ending -bhyaḥ added directly to the stem, as in रमाभ्यः, so विद्या becomes विद्याभ्यः.

<answer>विद्याभ्यः</answer>

The stem पूर्णापूर्णा is a feminine ā-stem. In the nominative singular, ā-stems keep the stem form unchanged, so the form is the stem itself.

<answer>पूर्णापूर्णा</answer>

Stem कज्जलिता is a feminine ā-stem. The nominative singular of such a stem is the stem itself, with no ending added.

<answer>कज्जलिता</answer>

Stem मृग is a masculine a-stem. The genitive plural of a-stems takes the ending -ānām, so मृग becomes मृगाणाम्.

The change from न to ण follows the retroflexion rule (ṇatva). The ṛ in the stem triggers it, and the intervening vowels and the ग do not block it. So मृगानाम् becomes मृगाणाम्.

<answer>मृगाणाम्</answer>

The stem पानीयाध्यक्ष ends in short -a, so it follows the regular masculine a-stem declension. In that declension the ablative plural ends in -ebhyaḥ (-एभ्यः).

Replacing the final -a with -e and adding -bhyaḥ gives पानीयाध्यक्षेभ्यः. The retroflex ष in the stem is already there, and no nasal in the stem is affected by retroflexion. The word contains न in पानीय, but it sits before the ष and is not in a position to be changed by the ending.

<answer>पानीयाध्यक्षेभ्यः</answer>

The stem रुधिराविला is a feminine ā-stem (रुधिर + आविला, "stained with blood").

For feminine ā-stems, the vocative dual is the same as the nominative and accusative dual, which ends in -e. Adding that ending to the stem gives रुधिराविले.

<answer>रुधिराविले</answer>

The stem चातुर्मासक ends in -a, so it declines like a regular masculine a-stem such as राम. The ablative singular of those stems ends in -āt, so चातुर्मासक becomes चातुर्मासकात्.

<answer>चातुर्मासकात्</answer>

The stem रेवत ends in short -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The nominative plural of a masculine a-stem ends in -āḥ, which gives रेवताः.

<answer>रेवताः</answer>

Taking मैरेय as a neuter a-stem, the dative singular ends in -āya, as in फलाय from फल.

Applying that ending to मैरेय gives मैरेयाय.

<answer>मैरेयाय</answer>

The stem युक्तार्था is a feminine ā-stem. The accusative plural of feminine ā-stems ends in -ās, as in रमाः from रमा. Adding that ending to the stem gives युक्तार्थाः.

<answer>युक्तार्थाः</answer>

I treated अनहा as a regular feminine ā-stem. The ablative dual of such a stem ends in -भ्याम्, so the form is अनहाभ्याम्. I could not match अनहा to a specific dictionary entry, so this rests on the ā-stem assumption.

<answer>अनहाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem भगल ends in short -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The nominative dual of a masculine a-stem ends in -au, giving भगलौ.

<answer>भगलौ</answer>

Stem कथ्य ends in -a, so it declines like राम. The ablative plural of a masculine a-stem takes -एभ्यः, giving कथ्येभ्यः.

<answer>कथ्येभ्यः</answer>

The stem स्पर्शिक ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular masculine a-stem such as देव. For these stems the vocative dual is the same as the nominative dual, which ends in -औ.

Adding -औ to the stem gives स्पर्शिकौ.

<answer>स्पर्शिकौ</answer>

Stem सांहितिक ends in -a, so it declines like a regular masculine a-stem such as देव. In the instrumental dual, देव gives देवाभ्याम्.

Applying the same pattern: सांहितिक + आभ्याम् gives सांहितिकाभ्याम्.

<answer>सांहितिकाभ्याम्</answer>

I took the stem वच to be a regular neuter a-stem. The ablative dual then takes the ending -भ्याम्, which lengthens the stem vowel to -ा, giving वचाभ्याम्. The stem could also be read as a truncated form of the s-stem वचस्, but I went with the a-stem as written.

<answer>वचाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem त्वेष्य ends in short -a, so it follows the neuter a-stem declension. In that declension the nominative dual ends in -े, the same ending as the vocative and accusative dual.

Adding it to the stem gives त्वेष्य + े = त्वेष्ये.

<answer>त्वेष्ये</answer>

The stem मर्दक is a masculine a-stem. For a-stems, the vocative dual is the same as the nominative dual, which ends in -au. Adding that ending to the stem gives मर्दकौ.

<answer>मर्दकौ</answer>

Stem स्यूत is a-stem, neuter. Ablative plural of a-stems: -ebhyaḥ, so स्यूतेभ्यः.

<answer>स्यूतेभ्यः</answer>

The stem क्रिया is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा. The locative plural ending of ā-stems is -āsu, which gives क्रियासु.

<answer>क्रियासु</answer>

The stem शम्बूक is a masculine a-stem. For a-stem masculines, the nominative dual ends in -au, as in राम → रामौ. Applying the same ending to शम्बूक gives शम्बूकौ.

<answer>शम्बूकौ</answer>

The stem व्याघ्रक is a masculine a-stem, so the accusative singular takes the ending -म्, giving व्याघ्रकम्.

<answer>व्याघ्रकम्</answer>

The stem मिष्ट is a masculine a-stem, so it declines like राम.

For the dative dual of an a-stem, the ending -भ्याम् attaches after the stem vowel is lengthened to -ए-. The stem मिष्ट therefore becomes मिष्टाभ्याम्.

The dative dual of राम is रामाभ्याम्, so the same pattern gives मिष्टाभ्याम्.

<answer>मिष्टाभ्याम्</answer>

Stem पीतावशेषा is a feminine ā-stem. The ablative dual of an ā-stem ends in -ābhyām, as in लताभ्याम्.

Adding this ending to the stem gives पीतावशेषाभ्याम्.

The stem षाड्वर्गिक ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem neuter noun. For these nouns the nominative and accusative plural are formed with -āni, which gives षाड्वर्गिकाणि.

<answer>अनिलात्मजाः</answer>

Stem फलिक is a masculine a-stem. The ablative dual of a-stems ends in -भ्याम्, with the stem vowel lengthened before the ending to -ए-: फलिक + भ्याम् → फलिकाभ्याम्.

Rule check: before an ending that begins with a bhi-type consonant (भ्याम्), a-stems change a to ā. So the form is फलिकाभ्याम्.

<answer>फलिकाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem शाप is a masculine a-stem, declined like राम. In the a-stem paradigm, the vocative dual is identical to the nominative dual, which ends in -औ.

Adding -औ to the stem gives शापौ.

<answer>शापौ</answer>

Neuter a-stem nouns form the nominative and accusative plural with -āni, so रोपित becomes रोपितानि.

<answer>रोपितानि</answer>

The stem करम्बित ends in -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem neuter. In the neuter dual, the locative takes the same ending as the genitive, -ayoḥ, which gives करम्बितयोः.

<answer>करम्बितयोः</answer>

Feminine ā-stem सामिषा takes the instrumental singular ending -ayā, so the form is सामिषया.

<answer>सामिषया</answer>

The stem वैमुक्त ends in short -a and is masculine, so it follows the regular a-stem declension. In that declension the vocative singular is the bare stem with the final vowel changed to -a, which here leaves the stem unchanged.

<answer>वैमुक्त</answer>

The stem आनुचारक ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem neuter noun. The neuter nominative plural of such stems ends in -āni, which gives आनुचारकानि.

<answer>आनुचारकाणि</answer>

Correction: the retroflex rule (ṇatva) does not apply here. The stem has the sequence र (r) followed by क and then आ, and the following न is separated from the र by क. Under the ṇatva rule, a र before a न turns it into ण only if no intervening consonant outside the allowed set (such as a velar like क) breaks the sequence. Velars (कवर्ग) do not block it. So the र in -चार- can still cause retroflexion across the intervening क.

Checking the sequence: in आनुचारकानि, the र is followed by आ, then क, then आ, then न. The vowel आ between them is allowed, and क is a velar, which also does not block. The rule applies when the र is in the same word and the न is in the inflectional ending, as in -āni. So the ending becomes -āṇi, as in चतुर्णाम् or the common pattern कारकाणि.

<answer>आनुचारकाणि</answer>

Stem: वैतालिन् is an n-stem ending in -in, masculine. In the dual, the nominative, vocative, and accusative all take the ending -au, so the stem वैतालिन् gives वैतालिनौ.

<answer>वैतालिनौ</answer>

The stem बभ्रुक ends in -a, so it declines like राम. In the masculine dual, the dative takes the same ending as the instrumental and ablative, -भ्याम्. Before this ending the stem-final -a lengthens to -ā, giving बभ्रुकाभ्याम्.

<answer>बभ्रुकाभ्याम्</answer>

Neuter a-stems form the nominative plural by adding -āni to the stem. The stem संधितव्य ends in -a, so the ending gives संधितव्यानि.

Internal sandhi could in principle change the final न् to ण्, but that happens only after ऋ, र् or ष् in the same word. The stem has त and व्य after the preceding syllables but no ऋ, र् or ष्, so the न् stays as it is.

<answer>संधितव्यानि</answer>

The stem द्वंद्व (dvandva) is a neuter a-stem. Neuter a-stems form the accusative singular with -म्, so the form is dvandvam.

The stem is written with an anusvara (द्वंद्व), so I kept that spelling: द्वंद्वम्.

<answer>द्वंद्वम्</answer>

The stem हट्ट is a masculine a-stem. The masculine accusative dual of an a-stem ends in -au, as in देवौ, so हट्ट becomes हट्टौ.

<answer>हट्टौ</answer>

The stem लोकानुकम्पक ends in -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The genitive singular of a masculine a-stem takes -स्य, giving लोकानुकम्पकस्य.

<answer>लोकानुकम्पकस्य</answer>

For a feminine long-ī stem declined like *nadī*, the ablative singular ends in -yāḥ. The final ī of माण्डपी becomes -y before the ending -āḥ, which gives माण्डप्याः.

<answer>माण्डप्याः</answer>

Feminine ā-stem चण्डा declines like रमा. The dative dual of such stems is formed with the ending -भ्याम्, so the form is चण्डाभ्याम्.

<answer>चण्डाभ्याम्</answer>

Stem मदालसा is a feminine ā-stem, declined like रमा. The dative dual of an ā-stem takes the ending -भ्याम् added to the stem with its final ā shortened to a, giving मदालसाभ्याम्.

For ā-stems, the instrumental, dative, and ablative dual all take -ābhyām, as in रमाभ्याम्. So the dative dual is मदालसाभ्याम्.

<answer>मदालसाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem सांवेषिका is a feminine ā-stem. For ā-stems, the dative dual ends in -ābhyām, so सांवेषिका becomes सांवेषिकाभ्याम्.

<answer>सांवेषिकाभ्याम्</answer>

Masculine a-stem nouns take the ending -भ्याम् in the ablative dual. The final -a of the stem lengthens before this ending, which gives भिल्लाभ्याम्.

<answer>भिल्लाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem श्यैनेय ends in short -a, so it follows the regular masculine a-stem declension. In that declension the vocative singular is the bare stem, as in राम → हे राम.

The vocative singular is therefore श्यैनेय.

<answer>श्यैनेय</answer>

Stem नूतना is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा. The genitive singular of रमा is रमायाः, and the same pattern gives नूतनायाः.

<answer>नूतनायाः</answer>

The stem पणितव्या is a feminine ā-stem, so I decline it like रमा. The vocative plural of such stems is the same as the nominative plural, which ends in -āḥ.

Adding -āḥ to पणितव्या gives पणितव्याः.

<answer>पणितव्याः</answer>

The stem आञ्छित ends in -a, so it declines like a regular masculine a-stem such as राम.

For the ablative plural, the a-stem takes the ending -ebhyas. The stem-final -a becomes -e before the bh- ending, giving आञ्छितेभ्यः.

<answer>आञ्छितेभ्यः</answer>

The stem कलम्बक is a masculine a-stem. The vocative plural of a-stems is the same as the nominative plural, which ends in -āḥ.

So कलम्बक becomes कलम्बकाः.

<answer>कलम्बकाः</answer>

The stem अङ्कित ends in short -a, so it declines like the regular masculine a-stem (as राम). The accusative singular of such stems takes the ending -am, which gives अङ्कितम्.

<answer>अङ्कितम्</answer>

The stem धावमाना is a feminine ā-stem. The accusative singular of such stems takes the ending -ām, giving धावमानाम्.

<answer>धावमानाम्</answer>

Neuter a-stem nouns take the ending -े in the nominative, vocative and accusative dual. Applying this to प्रेरक gives प्रेरके.

<answer>प्रेरके</answer>

The stem नवीना is a feminine ā-stem, so I take it as given. Feminine ā-stems such as रमा take no ending in the nominative singular, so the form is the stem itself.

<answer>नवीना</answer>

Stem उत्तराश्रित ends in -a, so it declines as a neuter a-stem. The neuter nominative singular of such stems takes the ending -m, which gives उत्तराश्रितम्.

<answer>उत्तराश्रितम्</answer>

The stem वैक्रिय ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular masculine a-stem such as राम. The accusative singular of that class takes -म्, which gives वैक्रियम्.

<answer>वैक्रियम्</answer>

Stem कामावसायिन् is an n-stem, so the ablative plural takes the ending -भ्यः added directly to the stem.

For the masculine n-stem, the ablative plural is formed from the stem with the final -न् dropped before a bhi- or bhyas-type ending. The same applies to words like राजन्, which gives राजभ्यः.

Dropping the -न् from कामावसायिन् gives कामावसायि-, and adding -भ्यः gives कामावसायिभ्यः.

<answer>कामावसायिभ्यः</answer>

The stem उदितानुवादिन् ends in -in, so it declines like other masculine in-stems (e.g. बलिन्).

In the dual, the ablative takes the same form as the dative and instrumental. For consonant stems this ending is -भ्याम्, added to the stem.

Before an ending beginning with भ्, the stem keeps its final न्. The pada stem is therefore उदितानुवादिन्, and the form is उदितानुवादिभ्याम्.

Because the stem ends in -in, the vowel before the न् is the short इ, which lengthens only in certain forms such as the nominative singular. In the -भ्याम् forms the stem's -इन् loses its न्, giving -इ-भ्याम्, as in बलिभ्याम्.

<answer>उदितानुवादिभ्याम्</answer>

Neuter a-stem nouns take -āni in the nominative, vocative and accusative plural. The vocative plural of प्लाव्य (plāvya) is therefore प्लाव्यानि (plāvyāni).

<answer>प्लाव्यानि</answer>

The stem साम्प्रदानिका is a feminine ā-stem, declined like रमा. For this class the accusative dual ends in -े (-e). So साम्प्रदानिका + े gives साम्प्रदानिके.

<answer>साम्प्रदानिके</answer>

The stem रोध ends in short -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The ablative dual of this class is formed with -ābhyām, where the stem-final -a lengthens to -ā before the bhyām ending: रोध + भ्याम् → रोधाभ्याम्.

<answer>रोधाभ्याम्</answer>

Following the standard feminine ā-stem paradigm (like रमा), the vocative dual is the same as the nominative dual, which ends in -े. Applied to the stem वालूका, this gives वालूके.

<answer>वालूके</answer>

The stem शमनीय ends in -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem. The neuter nominative singular of such a stem takes the ending -m, which gives शमनीयम्.

<answer>शमनीयम्</answer>

The stem तालिका is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा. The accusative singular of an ā-stem takes the ending -ाम्, which gives तालिकाम्.

<answer>तालिकाम्</answer>

I could not confirm the intended gender for this stem. वध्रिका ends in -ā and is normally feminine, so I declined it as an ā-stem. The accusative plural of an ā-stem is वध्रिकाः, and the masculine form of an ā-stem (as in सोमपाः) comes out the same way. If the stem were meant to be the masculine a-stem वध्रिक instead, the form would be वध्रिकान्.

<answer>वध्रिकाः</answer>

The stem रोगाख्य ends in short -a, so I decline it like a regular neuter a-stem such as फल. The dative singular of these stems takes -āya, which gives रोगाख्याय.

<answer>रोगाख्याय</answer>

The stem बल्बज is a masculine a-stem (a type of grass), so it declines like राम. The locative singular of an a-stem adds -े to the stem after dropping the final -अ.

बल्बज → बल्बजे

<answer>बल्बजे</answer>

The stem अर्थिक ends in -a, so it declines like राम. The masculine nominative singular of an a-stem takes -ः (visarga).

अर्थिक + सु → अर्थिकः

<answer>अर्थिकः</answer>

The stem पोषित ends in short -a and is masculine, so it follows the regular a-stem declension. The genitive singular of an a-stem adds -स्य to the stem.

पोषित + स्य = पोषितस्य

<answer>पोषितस्य</answer>

The stem विवन्दिषा is a feminine ā-stem (a desiderative abstract noun from vand). For ā-stems like रमा, the dual ablative takes the ending -bhyām, which is added to the stem with its final ā shortened to a, giving रमाभ्याम्.

So the form is विवन्दिषाभ्याम्.

<answer>विवन्दिषाभ्याम्</answer>

Feminine ā-stem घृताक्ता. The ablative plural takes the ending -भ्यः, with the stem vowel lengthened before bhyas in the ā-declension: -ābhyaḥ.

Ablative plural: घृताक्ताभ्यः

<answer>घृताक्ताभ्यः</answer>

Neuter a-stems take the ending -āni in the nominative and accusative plural. Here the stem पिण्ड gives पिण्डानि.

The retroflex ṇ already appears in the stem, so the rule that changes n to ṇ after ṛ, r, ṣ does not apply to the ending: the ending's n follows ḍ, which is not a trigger. The form is therefore पिण्डानि.

<answer>पिण्डानि</answer>

Stem तैजस ends in short -a, so it declines like the a-stem neuter noun फल. The neuter nominative and accusative plural of such stems ends in -āni, giving तैजसानि.

<answer>तैजसानि</answer>

The stem शुल्कोपजीविन् ends in -in, so it declines like other masculine -in stems such as बलिन्. In these stems the vocative plural is identical to the nominative plural, which is -इनः.

Replacing the final -इन् of the stem with -इनः gives शुल्कोपजीविनः.

<answer>शुल्कोपजीविनः</answer>

The stem स्वाध्यायन is a masculine a-stem. In the vocative dual, a-stems take the ending -औ, the same as the nominative dual, so the form is स्वाध्यायनौ.

<answer>स्वाध्यायनौ</answer>

Stem सिताभा is a feminine ā-stem, and the instrumental plural of such stems ends in -ābhiḥ.

सिताभा + भिः gives सिताभाभिः.

<answer>सिताभाभिः</answer>

The stem मृगव is a masculine a-stem, so the ablative singular ends in -āt.

<answer>मृगवात्</answer>

The stem रोमश ends in short -a and is masculine, so it follows the regular a-stem declension. The nominative singular of that declension ends in -aḥ (visarga), which gives रोमशः.

<answer>रोमशः</answer>

The stem कल्याणाभिनिवेशिन् is an n-stem ending in -in. Its masculine ablative plural is formed like the dative plural, with the ending -भ्यस् added to the stem.

Before a bha-initial ending, the stem keeps its final न्, which drops off as a pada-stem. So the form is कल्याणाभिनिवेशिभ्यः.

<answer>कल्याणाभिनिवेशिभ्यः</answer>

The stem लोहितोष्णीष is a masculine a-stem. In the vocative plural, a-stems take the same form as the nominative plural, which ends in -āḥ.

Stem: लोहितोष्णीष → lohitoṣṇīṣa
Vocative plural: lohitoṣṇīṣāḥ

<answer>लोहितोष्णीषाः</answer>

The stem सारि is a feminine i-stem. Like मति, it takes the locative dual ending -योः, and the final इ changes to य् before this vowel-initial-style ending, giving सार्योः.

<answer>सार्योः</answer>

Stem खादुका is a feminine ā-stem. The vocative plural of an ā-stem is the same as the nominative plural, which ends in -āḥ, so it is खादुकाः.

<answer>खादुकाः</answer>

The stem व्याघ्रादिनी is a feminine ī-stem declined like नदी. Its nominative plural is formed by changing the final ई to य् and adding ः, which gives व्याघ्रादिन्यः.

<answer>व्याघ्रादिन्यः</answer>

The stem सूचित ends in short -a, so it takes the regular a-stem neuter endings. In the plural, the ablative is identical to the dative, and both take -भ्यः. The stem vowel lengthens to -ए- before the -भ्यस् ending. This gives सूचितेभ्यः.

<answer>सूचितेभ्यः</answer>

The stem वर्णयितव्य ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem. For a neuter a-stem, the locative singular takes -े, the same as the masculine.

Adding -े to वर्णयितव्य gives वर्णयितव्ये.

<answer>वर्णयितव्ये</answer>

The stem क्षुल्ल ends in short -a, so it declines like the neuter a-stem noun फल. In the neuter, the nominative, accusative and vocative dual all take the ending -े (-e). Adding it to the stem gives क्षुल्ले.

<answer>क्षुल्ले</answer>

The stem इच्छा is a feminine ā-stem. Its dative plural takes the ending -भ्यः, with the stem vowel lengthened as in the other bhyas-forms (इच्छाभ्यः, like लताभ्यः).

<answer>इच्छाभ्यः</answer>

The stem मन्थरा is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा. The instrumental plural of such stems ends in -ābhiḥ, which gives मन्थराभिः.

<answer>मन्थराभिः</answer>

The stem वैदान्तिक ends in short -a, so it follows the regular masculine a-stem declension. In that declension the vocative singular is the bare stem, with no ending added (as in राम → हे राम).

<answer>वैदान्तिक</answer>

Taking वीणाला as a feminine ā-stem, the accusative dual follows the pattern of रमा, which gives रमे. By the same pattern, वीणाला becomes वीणाले.

<answer>वीणाले</answer>

Taking चिक्कणा as a feminine ā-stem, the locative dual follows the same pattern as रमा. The locative dual ending is -ओः, which gives चिक्कणयोः.

<answer>चिक्कणयोः</answer>

The stem वर्तनीय ends in -a, so the neuter follows the regular a-stem declension. The dative singular ending is -āya, which gives वर्तनीयाय.

<answer>वर्तनीयाय</answer>

Neuter a-stems take the ending -े in the nominative dual, as in फले. Applying this to the stem आनुपदिक gives आनुपदिके.

<answer>आनुपदिके</answer>

The stem रेचक ends in short -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The genitive singular of that paradigm adds -स्य to the stem.

रेचक + स्य = रेचकस्य

<answer>रेचकस्य</answer>

The stem यौषिण्य ends in -a and is neuter. Its genitive plural therefore takes the thematic ending -ānām, giving यौषिण्यानाम्.

The ending's न् does not become ण्. The retroflexing sounds ṣ and r are separated from it by ण्, which is not among the sounds that may intervene, so the rule is blocked. This parallels ब्राह्मणानाम्.

<answer>यौषिण्यानाम्</answer>

Stem मेघाच्छादिता is a feminine ā-stem, like रमा. The ablative dual of an ā-stem takes the ending -भ्याम्, so the stem vowel stays and the ending attaches directly, as in रमाभ्याम्.

मेघाच्छादिता + भ्याम् = मेघाच्छादिताभ्याम्

<answer>मेघाच्छादिताभ्याम्</answer>

Genitive plural of a neuter a-stem takes -आणाम्, giving पत्तरङ्गानाम् before sandhi adjustment. The र earlier in the word, with only a velar (ङ्, ग्) and a vowel intervening, triggers retroflexion of न to ण.

<answer>पत्तरङ्गाणाम्</answer>

The stem मेषिका is a feminine ā-stem. The accusative singular of an ā-stem ends in -ām, so मेषिका becomes मेषिकाम्.

<answer>मेषिकाम्</answer>

The stem मन्दक is a masculine a-stem. For a-stems, the instrumental dual ends in -ābhyām, and the final -a of the stem lengthens to -ā before the ending (as in देव → देवाभ्याम्).

Applying this to मन्दक gives मन्दकाभ्याम्.

<answer>मन्दकाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem गृहानुबद्धा is a feminine ā-stem. The accusative singular of an ā-stem takes the ending -ām, so गृहानुबद्धा becomes गृहानुबद्धाम्.

<answer>गृहानुबद्धाम्</answer>

I took the supplied stem गरीयसा as a feminine ā-stem, as the instructions say to use the supplied stem. Feminine ā-stems take the instrumental dual ending -ābhyām, which gives गरीयसाभ्याम्.

If the stem were read as the usual feminine of the comparative गरीयस्, namely गरीयसी, the form would instead be गरीयसीभ्याम्. I followed the stem as given.

<answer>गरीयसाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem तरिन् is an n-stem ending in -इन्. In the neuter, the nominative, accusative and vocative dual all take the ending -ई, which gives तरिनी. Because the न follows a र, with only the vowel इ between them, it becomes retroflex ण (as in करिणी).

<answer>तरिणी</answer>

The stem पुण्यक ends in -a, so it declines like a regular neuter a-stem such as फल. The dative singular of that class ends in -āya, which gives पुण्यकाय.

<answer>पुण्यकाय</answer>

The stem वाराणसेय ends in -a, so it is declined like राम (देव). The masculine dative singular of an a-stem takes -āya, which gives वाराणसेयाय.

<answer>वाराणसेयाय</answer>

The stem पुष्कला is a feminine ā-stem. For these stems the dual nominative, vocative and accusative all take the ending -े, so the vocative dual is पुष्कले.

<answer>पुष्कले</answer>

The stem वेन्य ends in short -a, so it follows the regular masculine a-stem declension. The locative singular of that declension ends in -e, which gives वेन्ये.

<answer>वेन्ये</answer>

The stem सून्नीय ends in -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem neuter noun. The nominative singular of such a neuter takes -m, giving सून्नीयम्.

<answer>सून्नीयम्</answer>

Taking the stem वलाहका as a feminine ā-stem, I use the regular ā-stem declension (like रमा).

The dative dual of an ā-stem ends in -ābhyām, so the form is वलाहकाभ्याम्.

<answer>वलाहकाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem चैत्रेय ends in -a, so it declines like the masculine a-stem राम. The nominative singular adds -स्, which becomes visarga, giving चैत्रेयः.

<answer>चैत्रेयः</answer>

The stem योज्य ends in short -a, so it follows the neuter a-stem declension. In that declension the nominative, vocative and accusative dual all take the ending -े (as in फले).

Replacing the stem-final -a with -े gives योज्ये.

<answer>योज्ये</answer>

Stem यौवराजिक ends in -a, so it declines like राम (अ-stem masculine).

The dative dual of राम is रामाभ्याम्. The final -a lengthens before the -bhyām ending, giving यौवराजिकाभ्याम्.

There is no ण-retroflexion issue here, since the ending's न is not involved.

<answer>यौवराजिकाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem पूज्य ends in short -a, so it declines like the neuter a-stem (e.g. फल). In the instrumental plural, the stem-final -a becomes -ai before the ending -bhis, which gives पूज्यैः.

<answer>पूज्यैः</answer>

The stem ललाट्य ends in -a, so it takes the regular a-stem neuter endings.

For the ablative plural, a-stem nouns use the -bhyaḥ ending with the stem vowel lengthened to -ai-. The stem ललाट्य becomes ललाट्य + एभ्यः, giving ललाट्येभ्यः. The ablative plural has the same form as the dative plural, and the neuter gender makes no difference in this case.

<answer>ललाट्येभ्यः</answer>

The stem मेघाच्छादिता is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा. In that paradigm the accusative plural ends in -ās, which becomes -ाः at the end of a word.

Applying this to the stem gives मेघाच्छादिताः.

<answer>मेघाच्छादिताः</answer>

The stem गलोद्भव ends in short -a, so it follows the regular masculine a-stem declension. The nominative plural of such stems ends in -āḥ, so गलोद्भव becomes गलोद्भवाः.

<answer>गलोद्भवाः</answer>

Stem अभिषेक्य is a masculine a-stem. The dative dual of a-stems takes -ābhyām, with the final -a lengthened to -ā-.

So अभिषेक्य + आभ्याम् gives अभिषेक्याभ्याम्.

Checking for sandhi: there is no retroflexion issue, since the nasal in -ābhyām is not affected. The stem has ष, but it is followed by e, and no n or ṇ appears in the ending that could change.

<answer>अभिषेक्याभ्याम्</answer>

The stem शौक्तिक ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem. In the neuter, the nominative, vocative and accusative dual all take the ending -ए.

Applying this to शौक्तिक gives शौक्तिके.

<answer>शौक्तिके</answer>

The stem पोषितव्य ends in short -a, so it takes the regular a-stem endings. In the neuter, the dative singular is formed like the masculine, with the ending -āya added to the stem.

पोषितव्य + आय = पोषितव्याय

<answer>पोषितव्याय</answer>

Feminine ā-stem उग्रा declines like रमा. The ablative plural of रमा is रमाभ्यः, so the form is उग्राभ्यः.

<answer>उग्राभ्यः</answer>

The stem गम्यमाना is a feminine ā-stem. In the nominative singular, ā-stems keep the stem form unchanged, as in रमा and लता.

<answer>गम्यमाना</answer>

The stem काश्मीरिक ends in -a, so it declines like a regular masculine a-stem such as राम.

For a masculine a-stem, the vocative plural has the same form as the nominative plural, which ends in -āḥ. Adding that ending to the stem gives काश्मीरिकाः.

<answer>काश्मीरिकाः</answer>

The stem श्लेषित ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem. A neuter a-stem takes -म् in the nominative singular, which gives श्लेषितम्.

<answer>श्लेषितम्</answer>

The stem शिष्टाशिन् is an -इन् stem. In these stems the genitive plural ending is -इनाम् in all three genders, so the neuter form is the same as the masculine.

The न् does not become ण्. Between the earlier ष् and this न् there are intervening sounds (ट्, श्) that block the retroflexion rule.

<answer>शिष्टाशिनाम्</answer>

The stem रोगाविष्टा is a feminine ā-stem. The nominative singular of an ā-stem is the bare stem, so no ending is added.

<answer>रोगाविष्टा</answer>

The stem संकेतित ends in short -a, so it declines like a neuter a-stem such as फल. The nominative plural of a neuter a-stem takes -āni, which gives संकेतितानि.

<answer>संकेतितानि</answer>

The stem सुखोत्सव ends in short -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The ablative singular of an a-stem ends in -āt, which gives सुखोत्सवात्.

<answer>सुखोत्सवात्</answer>

The stem तलातल ends in -a and is neuter. For a-stem neuter nouns, the nominative singular takes -म्, so the form is तलातलम्.

<answer>तलातलम्</answer>

Following the regular a-stem declension, the stem कराल takes the ablative plural ending -भ्यः. The final -a lengthens to -ā before this ending (the same change as in the dative plural), so कराल + भ्यः becomes करालेभ्यः. Since this is the ending -भ्यस्, the stem vowel actually becomes -e, as in the neuter and masculine plural of a-stems (e.g. वृक्षेभ्यः).

<answer>करालेभ्यः</answer>

Feminine ā-stem कृतोपचारा, dative dual. For ā-stems like रमा, the dative dual is रमाभ्याम्, so the form is कृतोपचाराभ्याम्.

<answer>कृतोपचाराभ्याम्</answer>

Masculine i-stem accusative singular: the stem अञ्जलि takes the ending -m, giving अञ्जलिम्.

<answer>अञ्जलिम्</answer>

The stem मुस्ता is a feminine ā-stem, declined like रमा. In this class the accusative dual ends in -े, so the form is मुस्ते.

<answer>मुस्ते</answer>

The stem इष्टि is a feminine i-stem. The accusative singular of a feminine i-stem takes the ending -म्, so इष्टि + म् gives इष्टिम्.

<answer>इष्टिम्</answer>

The stem वैधृता is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा.

For ā-stems, the nominative, accusative and vocative dual all end in -e, giving वैधृते.

<answer>वैधृते</answer>

The stem भरण्ड is a masculine a-stem. The dative plural of a-stems takes the ending -भ्यः, and the stem-final -अ lengthens to -ए before it (as in देवेभ्यः). That gives भरण्डेभ्यः.

<answer>भरण्डेभ्यः</answer>

Stem खेदित is a-stem (neuter), so the dative plural follows the a-stem pattern with the ending -भ्यः, where the stem-final a lengthens to ā before bh.

<answer>खेदितेभ्यः</answer>

Assuming आटक is an a-stem neuter noun, it declines like फल. The neuter nominative, vocative and accusative dual ends in -े, so the stem आटक takes this ending to give आटके. This holds in the vocative as well, since the vocative dual is identical to the nominative dual.

<answer>आटके</answer>

The stem दैवत्य ends in -a, so it declines like a regular neuter a-stem such as फल. The neuter dual for nominative, accusative and vocative ends in -े, so the accusative dual is दैवत्ये.

<answer>दैवत्ये</answer>

The stem दूषिका is a feminine ā-stem, declined like रमा. The vocative plural of an ā-stem is the same as the nominative plural, which ends in -āḥ.

Yaska (यस्क) is a masculine a-stem. The ablative dual of an a-stem ends in -ābhyām, as in देवाभ्याम्. Replacing the stem-final -a with -ābhyām gives यस्काभ्याम्.

<answer>यस्काभ्याम्</answer>

The stem दिवसान्तर ends in -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The vocative plural of राम is रामाः, which is the same as the nominative plural.

Applying this to the stem gives दिवसान्तराः.

<answer>दिवसान्तराः</answer>

The stem अवाप्त ends in short -a and is masculine, so it follows the regular a-stem declension. In that declension the accusative dual ends in -au, giving अवाप्तौ.

<answer>अवाप्तौ</answer>

Masculine a-stems form the vocative singular by using the bare stem, so छेद्य becomes छेद्य.

<answer>छेद्य</answer>

The stem गृह्य ends in short -a, so it declines like राम. The masculine dative singular of an a-stem ends in -āya, which gives गृह्य + आय = गृह्याय.

<answer>गृह्याय</answer>

The stem शङ्किल is a masculine a-stem. For a-stems, the vocative dual is identical to the nominative dual, which ends in -ौ. This gives शङ्किलौ.

<answer>शङ्किलौ</answer>

The stem कुपित ends in -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem. In the neuter nominative plural, a-stems take -आनि with a nasal insertion (e.g. फल → फलानि).

<answer>कुपितानि</answer>

The stem सापेक्षा is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा.

In the accusative dual, feminine ā-stems end in -े, as in रमे. Adding this ending to सापेक्षा gives सापेक्षे.

<answer>सापेक्षे</answer>

Following the regular a-stem declension, the instrumental plural of पण्डित (neuter) is पण्डितैः. In the instrumental plural, the stem-final -a combines with the ending -bhis to give -ais, so the form is the same in all three genders.

The stem गर्व is a masculine a-stem, so it declines like देव. The nominative plural of देव is देवाः, so the nominative plural of गर्व is गर्वाः.
