Correction: the nominative plural of a masculine a-stem ends in -āḥ only if the stem takes the long vowel, and for देव the form is देवाः (devāḥ), which is correct. For गर्व the same pattern gives गर्वाः. I wrote गर्वाः above, but the standard form is गर्वाः with ā, so the answer stands.

<answer>गर्वाः</answer>

The stem उत्पलाभ ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular masculine a-stem such as राम. The nominative dual of these stems ends in -औ, giving उत्पलाभौ.

<answer>उत्पलाभौ</answer>

Stem स्फुलिङ्गिन् is an n-stem (in-ending) in the masculine. The accusative singular of such stems adds -अम् to the stem with the final न् kept, as in दण्डिन् → दण्डिनम्.

<answer>स्फुलिङ्गिनम्</answer>

Stem सौवर्ण्य ends in -a, so it declines like a neuter a-stem such as फल. In the neuter, the vocative plural is the same as the nominative plural, which ends in -āni: सौवर्ण्यानि.

The stem शङ्कान्विता is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा.

The stem खादितव्य ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular masculine a-stem (e.g. राम). The nominative singular of such stems takes the ending -ः (visarga).

<answer>खादितव्यः</answer>

Feminine ā-stem कण्वीया declines like रमा. The nominative plural is the stem plus ः, giving कण्वीयाः.

<answer>कण्वीयाः</answer>

Taking विषास्वादा as a feminine ā-stem, the locative dual is formed like that of रमा, with the ending -योः added to the stem after its final ā becomes a: विषास्वादा → विषास्वादे. The ā-stem dual endings are -े for the nominative, vocative and accusative, and -ाभ्याम् for the instrumental, dative and ablative. The genitive and locative dual take -योः, which gives विषास्वादयोः.

<answer>विषास्वादयोः</answer>

Masculine a-stem धन्य takes the ablative dual ending -भ्याम्, with the stem vowel lengthened to -ए before it (as in देवाभ्याम्). Correction: in a-stems, the vowel before bhyām becomes -आ, not -ए. The instrumental, dative and ablative dual all take -आभ्याम्, as in देवाभ्याम्.

So धन्य + भ्याम् gives धन्याभ्याम्.

<answer>धन्याभ्याम्</answer>

The stem इत्वरी is a feminine long-ī stem, so I decline it like नदी. The locative singular of such stems ends in -ām, with the ī turning into य् before it. This gives इत्वर्याम्.

<answer>इत्वर्याम्</answer>

The stem सामासिक ends in -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem. The neuter dative singular of such stems ends in -āya, the same as the masculine.

सामासिक + आय = सामासिकाय

<answer>सामासिकाय</answer>

The stem धृषित ends in -a, so it declines like a regular masculine a-stem such as राम.

In the dual, the locative takes the same ending as the genitive: -ayoḥ. For a-stems this gives -योः, as in रामयोः.

Applying that to the stem, धृषित + योः gives धृषितयोः.

<answer>धृषितयोः</answer>

The stem मन्दानुसारिन् ends in -in, so it declines like other masculine -in stems such as बलिन्. The dative singular of these stems is formed by adding -ने to the stem after dropping the final न्.

The stem without the final न् is मन्दानुसारि, and adding -ने gives मन्दानुसारिणे.

The न् of -ने becomes ण् by retroflexion, because the preceding word contains ऋ, र् or ष् and the influence is not blocked. In मन्दानुसारिणे the ण is triggered by the र in -सारि-. Between the र and the न there are only the vowels ा and इ, which do not block it. The earlier न in मन्दा and in -नु- comes before the र, so it is unaffected.

<answer>मन्दानुसारिणे</answer>

The stem मुमूर्षा is a feminine ā-stem, which declines like रमा. The ablative plural of such stems ends in -ābhyaḥ, so मुमूर्षा becomes मुमूर्षाभ्यः.

<answer>मुमूर्षाभ्यः</answer>

Stem नाडिका is a feminine ā-stem, declined like रमा. The instrumental dual of an ā-stem takes the ending -ābhyām, giving नाडिकाभ्याम्.

<answer>नाडिकाभ्याम्</answer>

Jaraṭha is a masculine a-stem, so the genitive plural takes the ending -ānām: jaraṭha + ānām → jaraṭhānām.

<answer>जरठानाम्</answer>

The stem खादूरक ends in -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The vocative plural of a masculine a-stem is identical to the nominative plural, which ends in -āḥ.

खादूरक + आः gives खादूरकाः.

<answer>खादूरकाः</answer>

The stem त्रैपारायणिका ends in -ā, so it declines like a feminine ā-stem such as रमा.

For the dative dual, ā-stems take the ending -भ्याम्. The stem-final ā stays long before this ending, as in रमाभ्याम्.

Stem त्रैपारायणिका + भ्याम् gives त्रैपारायणिकाभ्याम्.

<answer>त्रैपारायणिकाभ्याम्</answer>

Stem रङ्क ends in -a, and the neuter accusative singular of an a-stem noun is the stem plus -m (-अम्), giving रङ्कम्.

<answer>रङ्कम्</answer>

Stem कूष्माण्ड is a neuter a-stem. In the neuter, the nominative, vocative and accusative plural all end in -āni, so the form is कूष्माण्डानि.

The retroflex ṇ already appears in the stem, so the rule that turns n into ṇ after ṛ, r or ṣ would apply here. The n of -āni follows ḍ, but ṇ and ḍ come after the r/ṣ trigger only if no intervening dental, palatal or other blocking sound occurs. In this stem the trigger is the ṣ in -ūṣ-. After it come ma, ṇ, ḍ, and then the ending. The stem has ṣ followed by m, then ā and ṇ and ḍ. The ending n would be separated from ṣ by the retroflex ṇ and ḍ, and the intervening sounds are not blockers (the labial m and vowels do not block, and ṇ and ḍ are retroflex). Normally, though, internal sandhi changes the ending n after ṣ, r or ṛ only when it is in the same word and no t-class, c-class, ś, l or similar sound intervenes. Here the intervening sounds are m, ā, ṇ, ḍ, ā, none of which are blockers, so in principle the ending n would become ṇ, giving कूष्माण्डाणि.

Checking the literature, the neuter plural of words like प्राण or कूष्माण्ड is given with ṇ when the retroflexion rule is met. The ṇ-conversion rule (ṛvarṇebhyo naḥ ṇaḥ, 8.4.1) requires the n to be in the same word, with ṛ, r or ṣ before it and any intervening sounds limited to vowels, guttural and labial consonants, y, v, h, and the like. Retroflex ḍ is not in that list of allowed intervening sounds. Retroflex ṇ and ḍ are t-varga counterparts of the "ṭ-varga" group, and intervention by the ṭ-varga blocks the change (8.4.2 and the rule about ṭu-class intervening). The ṭ-varga intervening (ṇ, ḍ) does block, so the ending stays n.

The form is therefore कूष्माण्डानि.

<answer>कूष्माण्डानि</answer>

The stem ध्मापित ends in -a, so it is declined as an a-stem neuter noun. The locative singular of such stems ends in -े, which gives ध्मापिते.

<answer>ध्मापिते</answer>

The stem ज्ञाप्य ends in short -a, so it is declined like the regular masculine a-stem (as in राम). The nominative singular of that class takes the ending -ः (visarga).

ज्ञाप्य + ः = ज्ञाप्यः

<answer>ज्ञाप्यः</answer>

Taking the feminine stem मेषा (ā-stem) as given, the accusative singular of an ā-stem ends in -ām, so मेषा becomes मेषाम्.

<answer>मेषाम्</answer>

The stem पल्लवापीडित ends in -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The ablative singular of an a-stem masculine is the stem plus -āt.

पल्लवापीडित + आत् → पल्लवापीडितात्

<answer>पल्लवापीडितात्</answer>

The stem मर्यादाचल ends in short -a and is masculine, so it follows the regular a-stem declension. The locative singular of an a-stem ends in -े (-e), so मर्यादाचल becomes मर्यादाचले.

<answer>मर्यादाचले</answer>

The stem वर्ग्य ends in -a, so it declines like a regular neuter a-stem. The neuter nominative plural of such stems ends in -āni, which gives वर्ग्य + आनि = वर्ग्याणि.

The change of न to ण follows from the retroflex rule. The preceding sounds are र् (in the conjunct र्ग्य) and then आ, and nothing blocks the rule, so न becomes ण.

<answer>वर्ग्याणि</answer>

The stem पिन्वमाना is a feminine ā-stem. Feminine ā-stems take no ending in the nominative singular, so the form is the stem itself.

<answer>पिन्वमाना</answer>

Vakra is a masculine a-stem. Its dative singular takes the ending -āya, so the form is vakrāya.

<answer>वक्राय</answer>

The stem सरल ends in short -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The accusative plural of राम is रामान्, so the accusative plural of सरल is सरलान्.

<answer>सरलान्</answer>

Stem सूतकिन् is an -in stem, masculine, and declines like गुणिन्. In the masculine accusative dual, -in stems take the strong-case ending -औ added to the stem form ending in -इन्. This gives सूतकिनौ.

<answer>सूतकिनौ</answer>

Stem हासिका is a feminine ā-stem. The ablative dual of such stems ends in -ābhyām, as in रमाभ्याम्. Replacing the final -ā of the stem with -ābhyām gives हासिकाभ्याम्.

One possible concern is the "ika" rule, by which a feminine stem in -ikā changes its i to a in the vocative singular only (as in हासिके). That does not affect this form.

<answer>हासिकाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem स्थूलोदरा is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा. In the dual, the nominative, vocative and accusative all take the ending -ए, which gives स्थूलोदरे.

<answer>स्थूलोदरे</answer>

The stem गुह्य ends in -a, so the neuter forms follow the pattern of फल. In that pattern the vocative singular is identical to the nominative singular, which ends in -m (-अम्). Here the vocative singular is therefore गुह्यम्.

<answer>गुह्यम्</answer>

Stem वैप्रश्निक is a masculine a-stem, so the dative singular takes the ending -āya (stem + आय).

Sandhi check: a + āya gives -āya, and the ṇatva rule does not apply, since the ending contains no retroflex trigger. <answer>रुदितम्</answer>

Taking पुष as a neuter a-stem, the locative singular is formed like देव → देवे, by adding -e to the stem. This gives पुषे.

<answer>पुषे</answer>

Taking क्षेत्रिय as a masculine a-stem, the ablative plural ends in -ebhyaḥ. The stem-final -a becomes -e before -bhyas, giving क्षेत्रियेभ्यः.

<answer>क्षेत्रियेभ्यः</answer>

The stem अन्योन्याश्रिता is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा. The vocative singular of such stems ends in -e, which gives अन्योन्याश्रिते.

<answer>अन्योन्याश्रिते</answer>

Stem बद्धानुशया is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा. The locative plural of रमा is रमासु, which gives बद्धानुशयासु.

<answer>बद्धानुशयासु</answer>

The stem दृढाङ्गा is a feminine ā-stem. For ā-stems, the accusative dual ends in -े, as in रमे from रमा. Adding that ending to the stem gives दृढाङ्गे.

<answer>दृढाङ्गे</answer>

This is based on reading the stem literally as an a-stem, अमिन (amina), not an in-stem. The masculine genitive plural of an a-stem adds -ānām, with the stem-final -a lengthened and the -n- of the ending retroflexed only where the rule requires it. Here no retroflexion applies, so the form is अमिनानाम्. If the stem were meant as the consonant stem अमिन् (amin), the form would instead be अमिनाम्.

<answer>अमिनानाम्</answer>

The stem अन्वयागत ends in short -a, so it follows the regular a-stem declension. In the neuter, the locative singular takes the same ending as the masculine, -e, added to the stem after dropping the final -a.

अन्वयागत → अन्वयागते

<answer>अन्वयागते</answer>

Declining पोषणीय as a masculine a-stem, the genitive singular takes the ending -स्य, which gives पोषणीयस्य. The ṇ in पोषणीय is already retroflex, and no sandhi changes it here.

<answer>पोषणीयस्य</answer>

Avekṣā is a feminine ā-stem. The ablative dual of an ā-stem ends in -ābhyām, as in latābhyām.

Adding this ending to the stem gives avekṣābhyām.

<answer>अवेक्षाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem चैत्य ends in short -a, and in the neuter it declines like फल. The dative singular of such stems ends in -āya, so चैत्य becomes चैत्याय.

<answer>चैत्याय</answer>

The stem वीषिता is a feminine ā-stem, so it takes the locative dual ending -योः, which gives वीषितयोः.

<answer>वीषितयोः</answer>

The stem हृतोत्तरा is a feminine ā-stem. The dative plural of an ā-stem takes the ending -bhyaḥ, as in रमाभ्यः, which gives हृतोत्तराभ्यः.

<answer>हृतोत्तराभ्यः</answer>

Feminine ā-stem प्रीता takes the locative plural ending -āsu, so the form is प्रीतासु.

<answer>प्रीतासु</answer>

The stem राष्ट्रीया is a feminine ā-stem. For ā-stems, the nominative dual ending is -े (e), the same as the accusative and vocative dual.

Applying this to the stem: राष्ट्रीया → राष्ट्रीये.

<answer>राष्ट्रीये</answer>

The stem व्यडम्बक ends in -a, so it declines like a regular neuter a-stem such as फल.

For neuter a-stems, the vocative plural is the same as the nominative plural, which ends in -āni. Adding this ending to व्यडम्बक gives व्यडम्बकानि.

The -n- of -āni would change to -ṇ- only if it followed ṛ, r, or ṣ within the same word without an intervening blocking sound. Here the stem contains ड and ब, but no ṛ, r, or ṣ. So the n stays as it is.

<answer>व्यडम्बकानि</answer>

The stem नाडिक ends in short -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The dative singular of the a-stem class ends in -āya, which gives नाडिकाय.

<answer>नाडिकाय</answer>

Stem योजनिक ends in a short -a, so it declines like a regular neuter a-stem such as फल.

For a neuter a-stem, the nominative and accusative plural take the ending -ानि. This gives योजनिकानि.

<answer>योजनिकानि</answer>

Taking मुख्य as an a-stem masculine noun, the ablative plural ends in -भ्यः. Before this ending, the stem-final -अ lengthens to -ए, as in देव → देवेभ्यः.

Applying the same rule to मुख्य gives मुख्येभ्यः.

<answer>मुख्येभ्यः</answer>

The stem नाटित ends in -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem neuter. In the ablative plural, a-stems take the ending -भ्यः, and the final -a lengthens to -ए- before it, giving नाटितेभ्यः. The neuter ablative plural is identical to the masculine one.

<answer>नाटितेभ्यः</answer>

I treated द्रु as a feminine short u-stem declined like धेनु. Such stems take the feminine dative singular ending -ै, with the final u becoming the semivowel व्. For धेनु this gives धेन्वै, and the same pattern applied to द्रु gives द्र्वै. This is a reasoned application of the धेनु paradigm; I did not check it against an attested form, since द्रु is more commonly neuter.

<answer>द्र्वै</answer>

The stem इभ्य ends in short -a, so it takes the regular a-stem endings. In the neuter, the instrumental plural is the same as in the masculine: the stem-final -a becomes -ai before the ending -ḥ (-भिः).

Instrumental plural: इभ्य + भिस् → इभ्यैः.

(The alternative ending -ebhiḥ, giving इभ्येभिः, is a Vedic form, so I use the classical form.)

<answer>इभ्यैः</answer>

The stem स्थायुक ends in -a, so it takes the regular a-stem ending for the genitive dual. That ending is -योः, and it is the same in the neuter as in the masculine. Adding it gives स्थायुकयोः. There is no न् in the form that could become ण्, so no retroflexion applies.

<answer>स्थायुकयोः</answer>

The stem सोमात्मक ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular neuter a-stem. The neuter accusative plural of such stems ends in -āni. No र, ष or ऋ precedes the न, so it does not become ण.

<answer>सोमात्मकानि</answer>

The stem अर्घार्हा is a feminine ā-stem, declined like रमा. In the dual, the nominative, vocative and accusative all take the ending -e.

So the vocative dual is अर्घार्हे.

<answer>अर्घार्हे</answer>

The stem वचनीय ends in short -a, so it declines like the neuter noun फल. The locative singular of a neuter a-stem is formed by adding -e to the stem, with the final -a dropped: वचनीय → वचनीये.

<answer>वचनीये</answer>

The stem श्वेत ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular neuter a-stem such as फल. In that paradigm the genitive singular ending is -स्य, which gives श्वेतस्य.

<answer>श्वेतस्य</answer>

Since कुम्भीकिन् is an -इन् stem, its neuter nominative singular drops the final न्, as in दण्डिन् → दण्डि.

<answer>कुम्भीकि</answer>

The stem रेचनक is a masculine a-stem. For a-stems, the vocative dual is the same as the nominative dual, which ends in -औ. Adding this ending to the stem gives रेचनकौ.

<answer>रेचनकौ</answer>

The stem लषित ends in -a, so it takes the regular a-stem neuter endings. The nominative singular of such a stem is the stem plus -m, which gives लषितम्.

<answer>लषितम्</answer>

Neuter a-stems form the locative singular with -e, as in फले from फल. Applied to उदुम्बर, this gives उदुम्बरे.

<answer>उदुम्बरे</answer>

The stem आभिज्ञानिक ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular masculine a-stem such as राम.

For the ablative singular of an a-stem, the ending is -āt, which gives आभिज्ञानिकात्.

<answer>आभिज्ञानिकात्</answer>

Neuter a-stems take the ending -े in the nominative, accusative and vocative dual. The stem शील therefore gives शीले in the accusative dual.

<answer>शीले</answer>

Stem मीना is a feminine ā-stem. The instrumental plural ending for ā-stems is -ābhiḥ, so the form is मीनाभिः.

<answer>मीनाभिः</answer>

The stem पलङ्कटा is a feminine ā-stem. In the vocative plural, ā-stems take the same form as the nominative plural, which ends in -āḥ. So पलङ्कटा becomes पलङ्कटाः.

<answer>पलङ्कटाः</answer>

The supplied stem कौण्डपायिना ends in -ā, so I treated it as a feminine ā-stem. Its instrumental dual takes the ending -ābhyām, giving कौण्डपायिनाभ्याम्. I kept the stem's dental न as supplied.

<answer>कौण्डपायिनाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem पाक्षपातिक ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem. In the neuter, the nominative plural of an a-stem takes -āni, giving पाक्षपातिकानि.

The -n- of -āni could in principle become -ṇ- by retroflexion (ṇatva), but the conditions are not met. The trigger would have to be ṛ, r, or ṣ earlier in the word, and the stem has ष् in पाक्ष. The intervening sounds, however, include क, a velar, and retroflexion by ṣ is blocked or not applicable here. The rule also needs the n to be in the same word after an uninterrupted sequence, and a ति sequence containing a dental t intervenes. The dental त् blocks the spread. So the n stays dental.

<answer>पाक्षपातिकानि</answer>

The stem स्फाटिकोपल ends in short -a, so it follows the regular masculine a-stem pattern. In the nominative singular, the final -a becomes -aḥ (visarga).

<answer>स्फाटिकोपलः</answer>

The stem मधुरानिरुद्ध ends in -a, so I declined it as a neuter a-stem. In the neuter dual, the nominative, accusative and vocative all take -े (-e). The vocative dual is therefore मधुरानिरुद्धे.

<answer>मधुरानिरुद्धे</answer>

The stem कुम्भोद्भव ends in -a, so it declines like a regular masculine a-stem noun such as राम. The nominative dual of such a noun ends in -au, which gives कुम्भोद्भवौ.

<answer>कुम्भोद्भवौ</answer>

Stem स्नेह is a-stem neuter. The ablative plural of a-stems ends in -ebhyaḥ, so the form is snehebhyaḥ (स्नेहेभ्यः).

<answer>स्नेहेभ्यः</answer>

Ablative plural of the feminine ā-stem लेखा takes the ending -भ्यः, the same as the dative plural, which gives लेखाभ्यः.

<answer>लेखाभ्यः</answer>

Stem जघन्या is a feminine ā-stem. The dative dual of ā-stems ends in -ābhyām, as in सेनाभ्याम्.

Adding this ending to the stem gives जघन्याभ्याम्.

<answer>जघन्याभ्याम्</answer>

Neuter a-stems form the nominative plural in -āni, so the stem उल्लापक becomes उल्लापकानि. The retroflex rule (नकार → णकार) does not apply here: the stem has no ऋ, र or ष before the ending, so the न stays as it is.

<answer>उल्लापकानि</answer>

The stem शिलोञ्छिन् is an in-stem (-इन्). Neuter in-stems form the nominative dual with -इनी, as in धनिन् → धनिनी. This gives शिलोञ्छिनी.

<answer>शिलोञ्छिनी</answer>

करालक is an a-stem neuter, so the locative dual takes the ending -योः, the same ending as the genitive dual. This gives करालकयोः.

<answer>करालकयोः</answer>

The stem हिडिम्बा is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा. The accusative plural of रमा is रमाः, so the form here is हिडिम्बाः.

<answer>हिडिम्बाः</answer>

Taking दन्त्य as a masculine a-stem (like राम), the genitive dual ending is -योः. The stem-final a lengthens to ā before this ending, as in रामयोः, giving दन्त्ययोः. Here the stem ends in -य, so the dual forms are दन्त्यौ (nominative) and दन्त्ययोः (genitive and locative).

<answer>दन्त्ययोः</answer>

The stem पल्लीश ends in short -a, so it is a masculine a-stem. Its nominative dual is formed like राम → रामौ, by adding -औ to the stem after dropping the final -a.

पल्लीश → पल्लीशौ

<answer>पल्लीशौ</answer>

Feminine ā-stem क्रान्ता declines like रमा. The locative plural of रमा is रमासु, so the form here is क्रान्तासु.

<answer>क्रान्तासु</answer>

Stem तूर्ण is a-stem (neuter). The nominative dual neuter of a-stems ends in -े, so the form is तूर्णे.

<answer>तूर्णे</answer>

The stem वैश्या is a feminine ā-stem, like रमा. The vocative singular of such stems ends in -e, as in हे रमे, so the form is वैश्ये.

<answer>वैश्ये</answer>

Taking the feminine stem स्प्रष्टव्या as an ā-stem, the instrumental plural ending is -ābhiḥ, which gives स्प्रष्टव्याभिः.

<answer>स्प्रष्टव्याभिः</answer>

The stem ताम्राभ ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem. The neuter ablative plural of an a-stem takes the ending -भ्यः, with the stem vowel lengthened before it to -ए-. This gives ताम्राभेभ्यः.

<answer>ताम्राभेभ्यः</answer>

The stem कौलीक ends in short -a, so it follows the regular masculine a-stem declension. The genitive singular of that declension takes the ending -स्य, which gives कौलीकस्य.

<answer>कौलीकस्य</answer>

The stem साभिताप ends in -a, so it is a regular masculine a-stem. The nominative singular of such a stem takes -ः (visarga).

<answer>साभितापः</answer>

The stem मार्जनीय ends in -a, so it declines like the thematic neuter stem फल. In the neuter, the vocative singular matches the nominative singular, which for a-stems is the stem plus -म्.

Vocative singular: मार्जनीयम्

<answer>मार्जनीयम्</answer>

The stem शिल्पा is a feminine ā-stem, declined like रमा. For these stems the dual in the nominative, vocative and accusative is the same form, ending in -e. The vocative dual is therefore शिल्पे.

<answer>शिल्पे</answer>

Neuter stems in -a decline like ज्ञान, so वाच्य takes the genitive singular ending -स्य, giving वाच्यस्य.

<answer>वाच्यस्य</answer>

The stem शुष्कक ends in -a, so it declines like the neuter a-stem noun फल. In that paradigm the vocative singular is the bare stem with the final vowel dropped and replaced by -a, which gives the same form as the nominative singular, -अम्. For neuter nouns the vocative singular is identical to the nominative singular. This gives शुष्ककम्.

<answer>शुष्ककम्</answer>

For a neuter i-stem, the nominative and accusative singular are both the bare stem, as in वारि. So the form is the stem itself.

<answer>सौम्याकृति</answer>

The stem भर्त्सना ends in -ā and is feminine, so it declines like रमा. The genitive singular of this class takes the ending -āyāḥ, which gives भर्त्सनायाः.

<answer>भर्त्सनायाः</answer>

The stem अनेकाश्रित ends in -a, so it declines like a regular masculine a-stem such as देव. For these stems the vocative dual is identical to the nominative dual, which ends in -औ.

Adding that ending to the stem gives अनेकाश्रितौ.

<answer>अनेकाश्रितौ</answer>

The stem पुलाकिन् is an n-stem ending in -in. In the masculine, the nominative plural of such stems is -इनः, and the vocative plural is identical to the nominative plural. Adding this ending to पुलाकिन् gives पुलाकिनः.

<answer>पुलाकिनः</answer>

Feminine ā-stem रसाढ्या declines like रमा. The instrumental dual of an ā-stem takes the ending -भ्याम् added to the stem with the final vowel shortened to -आ-, giving रसाढ्याभ्याम्.

<answer>रसाढ्याभ्याम्</answer>

The stem कृतोपचारा is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा. In that paradigm the accusative dual is रमे, so the corresponding form of this stem is कृतोपचारे.

<answer>कृतोपचारे</answer>

The stem योधनीया is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा.

For the ablative dual, ā-stems take the ending -bhyām, added to the stem with its final vowel lengthened or changed as the pattern requires. For रमा the ablative dual is रमाभ्याम्.

Applying the same pattern to योधनीया gives योधनीयाभ्याम्.

<answer>योधनीयाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem कम्पिल ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular masculine a-stem such as राम. The masculine accusative dual of राम is रामौ, so the same ending -औ applies here.

<answer>कम्पिलौ</answer>

The stem उक्थायु ends in -u, so it takes the regular u-stem endings. For the ablative dual, the ending is -भ्याम्, which attaches directly to the stem with no change. This is the same in all genders, so the feminine gives उक्थायु + भ्याम्.

<answer>उक्थायुभ्याम्</answer>

The stem वर्जा is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा. In that paradigm the accusative dual is रमे, and the same ending applied to this stem gives वर्जे.

<answer>वर्जे</answer>

The stem अधरा is a feminine ā-stem. The accusative singular of such stems ends in -ām, so अधरा becomes अधराम्.

<answer>अधराम्</answer>

The stem श्यामला is a feminine ā-stem, declined like रमा. For ā-stems, the instrumental dual ends in -ābhyām, so the form is श्यामलाभ्याम्.

<answer>श्यामलाभ्याम्</answer>

The stem लोकाभिलाषित ends in -a, so it declines like a regular masculine a-stem noun such as राम.

The ablative singular of an a-stem ends in -āt, so लोकाभिलाषित becomes लोकाभिलाषितात्.

<answer>लोकाभिलाषितात्</answer>

The stem करम्भ is a masculine a-stem. Instrumental dual for masculine a-stems takes the ending -ābhyām, as in देवाभ्याम्. So the stem's final -a lengthens to -ā and the ending -bhyām is added, giving करम्भाभ्याम्.

The ra in the stem does not trigger retroflexion of a following नत् (n), and no n appears in this ending anyway, so no sound change applies.

<answer>करम्भाभ्याम्</answer>

Stem सामीप्य ends in -a, and it is neuter. For a-stem nouns the ablative plural is formed like the dative plural, with -ebhyaḥ added to the stem.

सामीप्य + एभ्यः gives सामीप्येभ्यः.

<answer>सामीप्येभ्यः</answer>

Taking भक्कुर as a masculine a-stem, the dative dual ends in -ābhyām. The final -a of the stem lengthens before this ending, so भक्कुर becomes भक्कुराभ्याम्.

<answer>भक्कुराभ्याम्</answer>

Taking आत्मीया as a feminine ā-stem (like रमा), the genitive plural is formed by adding -नाम् to the stem, giving आत्मीयानाम्.

<answer>आत्मीयानाम्</answer>

I took the stem अञ्चति as a masculine i-stem noun declined like कवि (an assumption, since it could also be read as a participle). The genitive dual of such a stem ends in -योः (compare अग्नि → अग्न्योः). Here the final -इ turns into -य् before the ending -ओः, giving अञ्चत्योः.

<answer>अञ्चत्योः</answer>

Stem पतत्रिन् is an n-stem (in-stem), meaning "bird" (one with wings). Masculine genitive singular of in-stems (like बलिन्) is बलिनः.

So पतत्रिनः.

<answer>पतत्रिणः</answer>

Wait, I need to check whether the retroflex rule applies. In पतत्रिन्, the nasal न् follows ऋ/र/ष with no intervening blocking sounds? The rule (ṇatva) applies when न is in the same word after र, ष, ऋ, ॠ, with only vowels, velars, labials, ह, य, व, र, or anusvara between. Here the र is in त्रि, followed by इ and then न. The sequence र + इ + न: the vowel इ intervenes, which is allowed. So the न becomes ण: पतत्रिणः.

<answer>पतत्रिणः</answer>

The stem क्रियमाण ends in -a, so it declines like देव. The masculine locative plural ending is -एषु, giving क्रियमाणेषु.

<answer>क्रियमाणेषु</answer>

Neuter a-stem nouns take the dative singular ending -āya, the same as masculine a-stems. The stem प्रतीत ends in -a, so the dative singular is प्रतीताय.

<answer>प्रतीताय</answer>

Neuter a-stems form the nominative plural by adding -नि to the stem, with the stem vowel lengthened to -आ (as in फलानि, from फल).

For होम्य, the stem ends in -अ, so the nominative plural is होम्यानि.

<answer>होम्यानि</answer>

The stem अनुगेय ends in -a, so the neuter genitive singular follows the regular a-stem pattern (like फल → फलस्य).

Adding -स्य to the stem gives अनुगेयस्य.

<answer>अनुगेयस्य</answer>

Stem म्लेच्छितक ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem. In the neuter nominative singular, such stems take -m, giving म्लेच्छितकम्.

In the masculine locative singular the form is therefore कार्मुकिणि. The र् and म् also pose no problem, because labials do not block the change. The first न् does not appear in the form at all, because the stem's final न् is the one that becomes ण्.

<answer>कार्मुकिणि</answer>

The stem त्रुटित ends in short -a, so it follows the regular masculine a-stem declension.

Taking कच्छुरा as a feminine ā-stem, it declines like रमा. The dative plural of रमा is रमाभ्यः, so the form here is कच्छुराभ्यः.

The stem काल्याणक ends in -a, so it declines as a regular a-stem. In the neuter, the nominative plural of an a-stem ends in -āni (-आनि).

The retroflex ण in the stem does not change the ending's न, because the stem already contains ण before the ending and the न of -āni is separated from it by क. For the न to become ण by retroflexion, the intervening sound would have to be one that does not block the rule, and क is a velar. Velars (कवर्ग) do not block the rule. However, the trigger must be ऋ, र, or ष, and ण itself is not a trigger, so there is no retroflexion. The ending stays न.

<answer>काल्याणकानि</answer>

The stem घोराकारा is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा. The locative plural of an ā-stem takes the ending -सु, giving घोराकारासु.

The stem शाश्वतिक ends in -a, so it declines like a regular neuter a-stem such as फल. The neuter nominative and accusative plural of these stems ends in -āni, giving शाश्वतिकानि. No retroflexion of the n is needed, because there is no ṛ, r, or ṣ in the stem that would trigger it.

The stem श्लाक्ष्णभारिक ends in -a (the final -क with inherent a), so it declines like a regular masculine a-stem such as राम.

The stem पीतक ends in -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem. In the plural, the ablative takes the same ending as the dative, -bhyaḥ. Before this ending the stem-final -a lengthens to -e, giving पीतकेभ्यः.

The stem भूतोपहत ends in -a and is masculine. For a-stem masculines, the vocative plural is identical to the nominative plural, which ends in -āḥ.

Stem चूष्या is a feminine ā-stem. The instrumental plural of such stems takes the ending -ābhiḥ, as in रमाभिः.

<answer>चूष्याभिः</answer>

The stem शास्त्रोक्ता is a feminine ā-stem. For ā-stems, the nominative dual ending is -े (-e), as in रमा → रमे.

<answer>शास्त्रोक्ते</answer>

The stem कुण्डलाकार is an a-stem noun. Neuter a-stems take the same dative dual ending as masculines, -आभ्याम्, which gives कुण्डलाकाराभ्याम्.

Stem वैतनिक ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem neuter. The neuter nominative dual of such stems ends in -े, as in फले from फल. Adding that ending to वैतनिक gives वैतनिके.

The stem साध्य ends in short -a, so the neuter follows the regular a-stem pattern. The genitive singular of an a-stem takes -स्य, which gives साध्यस्य.

The stem वैवस्वतीय ends in -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem. For a neuter a-stem, the nominative singular takes the ending -m, giving the form with -अम्.

Stem दर्दरीक is a-stem (neuter). The neuter dual for nominative, vocative and accusative is -े: दर्दरीके.

<answer>दर्दरीके</answer>

Stem रथ्य ends in short -a, so it declines like the neuter a-stem राम/फल. In the dual, the ablative takes the same form as the dative and instrumental: -भ्याम्. Before a bhyām ending, a final -a lengthens to -ā, which gives रथ्याभ्याम्.

The stem पार्वत ends in -a, so it declines like राम. In the masculine, the ablative dual of a-stems is formed with -ābhyām, which replaces the stem-final -a with -ābhyām. This gives पार्वताभ्याम्.

The stem वैखानस ends in short -a and is masculine, so it follows the regular a-stem declension. The ablative singular of such stems ends in -āt: वैखानस + आत् gives वैखानसात्.

<answer>वैखानसात्</answer>

The stem स्निग्ध is a masculine a-stem, so it declines like राम. The genitive plural of the a-stem masculine is formed by adding -आनाम् to the stem without its final -अ, which gives स्निग्धानाम्.

The stem नष्टा is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा. The nominative plural of an ā-stem ends in -āḥ, which gives नष्टाः.

The stem औजसिका is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा. The nominative plural of such stems ends in -ाः, which gives औजसिकाः.

Stem स्थापिन् is an n-stem ending in -in. Before the bh- endings of the dative plural, the final -न् drops, so the form is स्थापिभ्यः, the same as for पक्षिन् → पक्षिभ्यः.

The stem कर्कर ends in short -a, so it follows the regular a-stem neuter declension. In that declension the dative singular ending is -āya, the same as in the masculine.

Taking चला as a feminine ā-stem like रमा, the locative plural ends in -āsu. The stem चला + सु gives चलासु.

The stem शताधिका is a feminine ā-stem, declined like रमा. For this class the genitive dual ends in -योः, so शताधिका + योः gives शताधिकयोः.

The stem अल्प is an a-stem, and the neuter locative singular of a-stems takes the ending -े, the same as the masculine form (the ending is -इ, which combines with the stem-final अ to give ए).

The stem पारणीय ends in -a, so it declines like the a-stem neuter noun. The neuter accusative singular of an a-stem takes -m, giving पारणीयम्.

The stem आग्नापौष्ण ends in -a, so it declines like a regular masculine a-stem noun. The locative plural of such stems is formed by changing the final -a to -e and adding -षु (-ṣu). This gives आग्नापौष्णेषु.

Assuming क्षुल्ल is a regular a-stem, the neuter locative singular takes the ending -े, as in फल → फले.

The stem क्षुभित ends in short -a, so it follows the regular a-stem neuter paradigm. The dative singular of that paradigm ends in -āya, giving क्षुभिताय.

<answer>क्षुभिताय</answer>

The stem लब्धव्य ends in short -a and is neuter. For a-stem neuters, the nominative, vocative and accusative dual all take the ending -े, so the form is लब्धव्ये.

The stem मोहनक ends in short -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The dative singular of an a-stem ends in -āya, which gives मोहनकाय.

<answer>चाञ्चल्यम्</answer>

Stem कर्पटि is an i-stem masculine noun. The nominative plural of masculine i-stems ends in -अयः, so the form is कर्पटयः.

The stem दयान्वित ends in -a, so it declines like a regular masculine a-stem such as देव. In the dual, the ablative takes the ending -भ्याम्. Before this ending the final -a lengthens to -ā, which gives दयान्विताभ्याम्.

The stem उपान्त ends in -a and is masculine. The nominative dual of a masculine a-stem is formed with the ending -au, so उपान्त becomes उपान्तौ.

The stem हीरक is a masculine a-stem, so it declines like राम. The nominative plural of a masculine a-stem ends in -āḥ, which gives हीरकाः.

The stem धूपायित ends in -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The vocative dual of a masculine a-stem is the same as the nominative dual, which ends in -औ.

The stem वैभातिक ends in short -a, so it declines like the regular masculine a-stem राम. The genitive singular of such stems ends in -स्य, which gives वैभातिकस्य.

The stem मदोन्मत्त ends in short -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The dative singular of that class ends in -आय.

The stem भेदिका is a feminine ā-stem. The locative plural of ā-stems takes the ending -āsu, so भेदिका + सु gives भेदिकासु. No sandhi or retroflexion applies here, since the stem has no ṇ-conditioning environment before the ending and the s follows ā rather than a retroflex-triggering vowel.

Kuḍmala is a neuter a-stem, so the nominative plural takes -āni with the nasal insertion (nuṃ): kuḍmala + āni gives kuḍmalāni.

The stem क्षेम is a masculine a-stem, so the ablative singular takes the ending -āt, as in राम → रामात्.

<answer>क्षेमात्</answer>

The stem चूडाला is a feminine ā-stem. The locative dual of such stems takes the ending -योः, like रमा → रमयोः.

Neuter a-stem nouns take -āni in the nominative plural, so रन्ध्र becomes रन्ध्राणि. <answer>रन्ध्राणि</answer>

The stem डल्लक ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular masculine a-stem such as राम.

For the dative plural of these stems, the ending -भ्यः is added and the final -a lengthens to -ā-, for example रामेभ्यः. Applying this to डल्लक gives the form below.

<answer>डल्लकेभ्यः</answer>

The stem पौत्रिक ends in short -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The accusative singular of that pattern takes -म्, giving पौत्रिकम्.

<answer>पौत्रिकम्</answer>

The stem जटिन् is an n-stem, declined like बलिन् or दण्डिन्. In the dative singular, the ending -े is added to the bare stem, giving जटिने.

<answer>जटिने</answer>

गोपिका is a feminine ā-stem, and the vocative plural of such stems is identical to the nominative plural. The nominative plural of गोपिका is गोपिकाः, so the vocative plural is the same.

The stem क्षीराह्वय is a masculine a-stem, so the genitive plural ending is -नाम् added after lengthening the final -a to -ā (क्षीराह्वया + नाम्). The र in क्षीर triggers retroflexion of the न. Only आ, ह्, व् and य intervene, and none of these blocks the change, so न becomes ण.

<answer>क्षीराह्वयाणाम्</answer>

The stem सांशयिक ends in -a, so it declines like a regular neuter a-stem. In that declension the nominative, accusative and vocative dual all take the ending -े, which gives सांशयिके.

The stem यजमानक ends in short -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The genitive singular of that class takes -स्य, giving यजमानकस्य.

The stem मोदनीय ends in -a, so it declines like राम. In the masculine, the vocative dual is identical to the nominative dual, which is the stem plus -औ.

The stem गृहाश्रमिन् is an n-stem ending in -इन्, so it declines like इन्-stems such as योगिन्.

The stem ज्ञानोल्का is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा. The instrumental plural of रमा is रमाभिः, so the form here is ज्ञानोल्काभिः.

The stem स्थिरानुरागा is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा.

The stem सेन्द्र is a masculine a-stem. Its locative dual takes the ending -योः, with the stem's final -a lengthened to -e before it, as in देवयोः. This gives सेन्द्रयोः. There is no nasal after the ऋ/र/ष trigger, so no retroflexion (ṇatva) applies.

<answer>सेन्द्रयोः</answer>

The stem अवाप्तव्य ends in short -a and is masculine, so it follows the regular a-stem declension. In that declension the vocative plural is identical to the nominative plural, which ends in -āḥ for masculines of this type: अवाप्तव्य + आः gives अवाप्तव्याः.

Stem स्यन्दनारूढ ends in -a and is masculine. Its vocative dual is the same as the nominative dual, which for a-stems is -au.

Shikhaṇḍa is a masculine a-stem. The vocative dual of a masculine a-stem is the same as the nominative dual, which ends in -au. This gives शिखण्डौ.

Stem खण्डक is a neuter a-stem. The genitive plural of a-stem nouns ends in -ānām, so the form is खण्डकानाम्. <answer>खण्डकानाम्</answer>

The stem उपवासिन् is an n-stem, so the dative dual takes the ending -भ्याम् added to the stem.

Before a bha-initial ending, the stem-final न् is a pada-final consonant and drops: उपवासिन् + भ्याम् → उपवासिभ्याम्.

The stem कामन्दक ends in -a and is masculine. For a-stem masculine nouns, the vocative singular is the bare stem, so the form is कामन्दक.

The stem मुहूर्तक ends in short -a, so it declines like a neuter a-stem such as फल. Stem यतितव्य ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem neuter. In the ablative plural, a-stems take -ebhyaḥ, which gives यतितव्येभ्यः.

<answer>यतितव्येभ्यः</answer>

The stem कुरुम्बा is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा. The vocative plural of such stems is identical to the nominative plural, which ends in -āḥ. This gives कुरुम्बाः.

The stem पाक्ष ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular masculine a-stem such as राम. The genitive dual of that class is formed with -योः, giving पाक्षयोः. No sandhi change or retroflexion (ṇatva) applies here.

The stem यतितव्या is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा. In the accusative plural, the stem-final -ā becomes -ās, which gives यतितव्याः.

The stem वृद्ध ends in -a, so it declines like a regular neuter a-stem. For these stems the instrumental plural is formed with -ais, the same as the masculine, giving वृद्धैः.

The stem स्तोतव्य ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular masculine a-stem such as देव.

The stem सांव्यवहारिक ends in -a, so it declines like a regular masculine a-stem such as राम. The vocative singular of such stems is the bare stem, giving सांव्यवहारिक.

Stem मुण्डिका is a feminine ā-stem. The genitive plural of ā-stems takes the ending -नाम् (as in रमा → रमाणाम्), formed by adding -ānām to the stem.

<answer>मुण्डिकानाम्</answer>

I took the supplied stem वर्ष्म as a neuter a-stem. The locative plural of a-stems ends in -एषु, which gives वर्ष्मेषु. (If the stem were the n-stem वर्ष्मन्, the form would instead be वर्ष्मसु.)

The stem प्रौढाचार ends in short -a and is masculine, so it follows the regular a-stem declension. The nominative singular of such stems takes -ः (visarga).

The stem बल्लवी ends in long ई and is a feminine noun of the nadī type (it is not monosyllabic, so it does not follow the dhī/śrī pattern).

The stem तुष्टि is a feminine i-stem. In the dual, the nominative, vocative and accusative share one ending, which for i-stems gives -ī. So the accusative dual is तुष्टी.

The stem भुजंगाख्य is a masculine a-stem, so the instrumental singular takes the ending -ena (अ + एन → एन). There is no र, ष or ऋ earlier in the word to trigger retroflexion, so the न stays dental.

Stem कृतार्थ ends in short -a, so it declines like राम. In the masculine, the ablative dual takes the ending -भ्याम्, and the stem-final -a lengthens to -ā before an ending beginning with भ्. This gives कृतार्थाभ्याम्.

The stem भागवताष्टक ends in -a and is neuter, so it declines like फल. The accusative singular of a neuter a-stem takes the ending -म्, which gives भागवताष्टकम्.

<answer>भागवताष्टकम्</answer>

The stem आष्टकीय ends in -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem. In the neuter, the nominative, vocative and accusative plural all take -ानि.

The stem कलहाकुला is a feminine ā-stem, so it declines like रमा. The dative plural of रमा is रमाभ्यः, so the ending -भ्यः is added to the stem with its final ā kept.

Feminine ā-stem उच्चावचा declines like रमा. The accusative dual of an ā-stem ends in -े, so the form is उच्चावचे.

Since कार्कन्धव is an a-stem, its neuter vocative singular is the bare stem, with no -m ending (unlike the nominative and accusative, which take -am).

<answer>कार्कन्धव</answer>

The stem उत्सङ्गिनी is a feminine stem ending in long ī, formed from उत्सङ्गिन्. It declines like नदी, a feminine ī-stem that is not monosyllabic.

This is a masculine a-stem noun. The instrumental dual ending is -ābhyām, which replaces the final -a of the stem: माणिक्यान्तक → माणिक्यान्तकाभ्याम्. The ण in the stem does not cause any retroflex change, and the ending contains no न to be affected.

Stem औरसिक ends in -a, so it takes the regular masculine a-stem endings. The ablative dual of an a-stem is formed with -ābhyām, as in रामाभ्याम्.

The stem उल्क ends in short -a, so it follows the regular masculine a-stem declension. In the dative plural, the stem-final -a becomes -e before the ending -भ्यस्, giving उल्केभ्यः.

The stem मुषितक ends in short -a, so it declines like a regular a-stem neuter. The genitive singular of such stems takes the ending -स्य, which gives मुषितकस्य.

The stem मालव is a masculine a-stem, so it takes the a-stem dative singular ending -āya.

The stem अतीन्द्रिया is a feminine ā-stem, and these stems take -āyai in the dative singular, giving अतीन्द्रियायै.

The stem अविका ends in -ā, so it takes the feminine ā-stem declension. In the nominative singular this ending leaves the stem unchanged.

The stem जङ्घिल ends in -a, so it declines like a regular neuter a-stem such as फल.

The stem गुल्म is a masculine a-stem. The instrumental singular of such stems takes the ending -ेन, giving गुल्मेन.

The stem मेलक ends in short -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The locative singular of that class ends in -e, giving मेलके.

The stem चलित ends in -a and is masculine, so it declines like राम. The genitive singular of a-stem masculines ends in -स्य, which gives चलितस्य.

This holds in the standard grammars (nadyau).

<answer>अनुवाकानुक्रमण्यौ</answer>
